deltas.title: Per-example telemetry runs before the promotion it can preempt
deltas.what: Ours interposes a full extra forward pass over the dev set (per_example_eval.collect_per_example_losses, one no_grad forward per eval batch) plus two JSONL appends BETWEEN the eval metric and the best-checkpoint promotion. Its own comment at line 715-716 says 'LOGGING ONLY - nothing below reads this'. The boss promotes first and has no such block anywhere in on_evaluate.

That 0.0010 is one seventh of the 0.0072 gap to rank 1 on that task, bought back for free. On a slower model the same block eats the entire end_time window and the deadline eval never promotes at all.

Nothing in scripts/ or ops/ ever reads that file - the only other references SET the path in smoke scripts. telemetry.load's own docstring says 'For offline analysis, not used in training'. output_dir is not the submission dir, so the file dies with the container. deltas.title: Our KL checkpoint metric costs two extra dev passes per eval; the boss's costs zero
deltas.what: Ours computes the validator's weighted metric (eval_loss + kl_coef*KL) by calling kl_metric_fn from inside CustomEvalSaveCallback.compute_loss - the very first statement of on_evaluate. That function loops the whole eval dataloader running the model twice per batch (adapter on, then under disable_adapter). The boss reaches the same weighted number for free: it adds the KL term inside the TRAINING compute_loss, which HF's prediction_step also calls, so metrics['eval_loss'] already carries the KL and the callback's compute_loss is a plain dict lookup.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/customized_trainer.py:311-363 (compute_loss, called at :691 before everything) and the metric fn at /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/train_instruct.py:691-714 (two forwards per batch over the full eval loader), wired at :716-717
deltas.theirs: BOSS/scripts/customized_trainer.py:98-103 - compute_loss is `metrics.get("eval_loss")`, no I/O, no forward pass. The KL lives in BOSS/scripts/kl_trainer.py:127-183 (returns `(loss, outputs)` at :183 so prediction_step uses it), wired at BOSS/scripts/train_instruct.py:501,534-537.
deltas.cost_if_wrong: On a KL-flagged instruct task each eval pays THREE full dev passes before promotion (KL x2 + per-example x1) against the boss's zero. Combined with delta 4 the eval cadence never widens to compensate. On the deadline eval this is the difference between promoting the last checkpoint and being killed mid-measurement.
deltas.recommendation: Port the boss's placement: put the KL term in the trainer's compute_loss (we already have scripts/kl_trainer_mixin.py:79-100 doing exactly this) and make the callback read eval_loss directly. Delete kl_metric_fn and the retry/inf-fallback ladder at 337-363 with it.

deltas.title: The boss has two eval-cost governors we removed and never replaced
deltas.what: The boss cancels evals before 0.75 epochs on multi-epoch runs (cancelling should_evaluate AND should_save, with an explicit carve-out so the one-shot end_time save is never cancelled), and after the first real eval it measures eval_runtime, budgets 10% of the remaining wall-clock for evals, and WIDENS args.eval_steps/save_steps accordingly (never shrinks). We have neither. So we made each eval roughly 3x more expensive and simultaneously deleted the mechanism that would have thinned the cadence to pay for it.
deltas.ours: ABSENT - grep for '_eval_timing_adjusted' and '0.75' over /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/customized_trainer.py returns nothing; on_step_end ends at :630 with no cadence logic and on_evaluate ends at :877 with no runtime measurement.
deltas.theirs: BOSS/scripts/customized_trainer.py:231-245 (skip evals before 0.75 epochs, never on reason=='end_time') and :272-295 (measure eval_runtime, max_evals from a 10% budget, widen eval_steps/save_steps)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Every minute spent evaluating is a minute not training, and on our side each eval is now several dev passes. On a long run this is the compounding form of delta 1 - not one lost checkpoint but a materially smaller step count for the same budget.
deltas.recommendation: Port both blocks verbatim from BOSS 231-245 and 272-295. They are self-contained, read-only against the rest of our callback, and the second one directly bounds the cost the per-example block added.

deltas.title: The architecture restore is a per-save net for the boss and a single post-training line for us
deltas.what: The boss patches config.json['architectures'] back to the base model's value inside on_save, at BOTH copy sites, every time the submission is written. We have the identical logic but call it exactly once, after run_training() returns. Our own comment in this file says a submission whose architectures do not match fails the validator's is_finetune check outright - and on the gemma run run_training() never returned, so it never ran.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/customized_trainer.py:917-952 - both copy sites, NO patch call. The logic exists at /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/text_trainer.py:696-717 and is invoked once at :1402, after training. The risk is spelled out in our own comment at customized_trainer.py:583-590.
deltas.theirs: BOSS/scripts/customized_trainer.py:78-96 (_patch_submission_architectures, config cached in __init__ at :66-73) called at :319 (save_only path) and :344 (best-checkpoint path)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Not ranks - the entry. A run killed or crashed before text_trainer.py:1402 ships a submission the validator can reject. The boss's placement is structurally immune because the patch happens at the moment the artefact is written.
deltas.recommendation: Port _patch_submission_architectures into the callback (cache the base config in __init__, call it right after each copytree at 924 and 948). Keep the post-training call as a second net - it also covers the add_random_noise fallback path, which the callback does not.

deltas.title: Cross-instance best-checkpoint persistence can suppress the submission write entirely
deltas.what: On construction we restore best_checkpoint_info {step, loss} from a Redis key written by a PREVIOUS trainer subprocess. Promotion then requires beating that foreign number. If the final run's evals never beat a loss recorded by a different attempt at a different learning rate, update_best_checkpoint is never set, on_save's copy branch never fires, and this run writes nothing to submission_dir. The key is cleared only when a whole new task starts, never between attempts. The boss has no persistence at all - every process starts with best_checkpoint_info=None, so its first eval always promotes and always writes the submission.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/customized_trainer.py:252-273 (restore) and :784-791 (write). Promotion gate at :769; copy branch at :936-952. State cleared only at /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/text_trainer.py:1119-1120, at task start. Key is the single global 'state' (scripts/state_manager.py:4), so it survives across attempts within a task.
deltas.theirs: BOSS/scripts/customized_trainer.py:54-56 - `self.current_best_loss = None; self.best_checkpoint_info = None; self.update_best_checkpoint = False`. ABSENT: no read of, or write to, any persisted best-checkpoint key anywhere in BOSS/scripts.
deltas.cost_if_wrong: A silent zero. The run trains, evaluates, finishes cleanly and leaves submission_dir holding whatever a previous attempt left there - or nothing. It cannot be distinguished from a healthy run in the logs, because nothing prints when a promotion simply does not happen. (Code path is MEASURED at the lines above; the live failure is INFERRED - it needs a probe run to have reached an eval before its checking_step.)
deltas.recommendation: Delete the restore at 252-273. The stated purpose (stop a worse final run overwriting a better probe run) does not hold: probe runs launch with save_strategy=no and their output_dir is per-attempt, so the checkpoint the restored loss refers to usually is not on disk under this run's output_dir at all. Keep the write at 784-791 only if something reads it; today nothing does.

deltas.title: GRPO never evaluates - checkpoints are selected on a training-log proxy
deltas.what: We set _grpo_no_eval=True on the GRPO subclass, which makes on_step_end force save-only and cancel every eval. grpo_config passes --eval_strategy no, so nothing else can trigger one. Consequence: on_evaluate never fires for GRPO, GRPOCustomEvalSaveCallback.compute_loss is dead code, best_checkpoint_info is never populated, and selection is entirely the _h3_last_proxy gate in on_save - fed from TRAINING logs. The boss's GRPO callback evaluates and ranks on eval_reward and eval_kl taken from the eval metrics. Both repos pin trl==0.18.0 on the identical line, so the TRL crash our comment cites is not a version difference between us and the boss.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/customized_trainer.py:1314 (_grpo_no_eval=True), :550-562 (forces save-only, cancels eval), :901-916 (selection on _h3_last_proxy from on_log), :1619-1652 (compute_loss, unreachable). /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/grpo_config.py:213 '--eval_strategy no'. /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/training_requirements.txt 'trl==0.18.0'.
deltas.theirs: BOSS/scripts/customized_trainer.py:354-394 - GRPOCustomEvalSaveCallback.compute_loss reads eval_reward and eval_kl from metrics/log_history and returns -(reward - 0.5*kl); on_step_end :210-229 sets control.should_evaluate=True for GRPO exactly as for instruct. BOSS/scripts/grpo_config.py:208 same '--eval_strategy no'. BOSS/scripts/training_requirements.txt 'trl==0.18.0'.
deltas.cost_if_wrong: This is the same class of bug as the DPO probe-loss one we already fixed for instruct: selecting on the signal that rewards fitting the training set. On GRPO, where higher wins and the metric is reward minus 0.5*KL, a training-log proxy has no held-out anchor at all.
deltas.recommendation: Reproduce the claimed trl 1199 reshape crash under trl==0.18.0 with our GRPO eval config before keeping the workaround. If it is real it is a batch/num_generations divisibility problem in OUR eval config, not in TRL - fix the config and restore eval-based selection to match BOSS 354-394. If it does not reproduce, delete _grpo_no_eval outright.

deltas.title: Our WSM merge is a weaker construct than the boss's greedy soup, and it is unbounded in time
deltas.what: Both sides average checkpoints, but the mechanisms differ in every way that matters. Ours copies up to K=3 full checkpoint DIRECTORIES to a disk pool, averages all K at equal weight in one shot, evaluates the result once and accepts or rejects the whole thing; LoRA only; no time bound. The boss keeps snapshots in RAM under an explicit free-RAM admission test, then runs a GREEDY soup seeded at the best single - it adds one candidate at a time and keeps it only if dev loss drops, so the outcome is monotone by construction, never worse than the best single, and it stops when half the remaining wall-clock is spent. The boss also handles full fine-tunes and sharded models via a disk-averaging fallback, and persists with a weights-only atomic swap.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/customized_trainer.py:284-309 (config), :954-967 (track on save), :974-1042 (disk copytree pool), :1044-1204 (one-shot equal-weight merge + single accept/reject at :1187), :1231-1247 (on_train_end trigger, no time check). LoRA-only bail at :984-1002.
deltas.theirs: BOSS/scripts/checkpoint_avg_callback.py:199-209 (RAM admission), :211-239 (pool), :261-332 (greedy soup: seed at best :277-279, accept only if `cand_loss < best - 1e-6` :305, time budget half the remaining wall-clock :287-296), :349-455 (disk fallback for sharded/large), :757-775 (restore best + weights-only atomic swap). Wired at BOSS/scripts/train_instruct.py:485-495, final run only.
deltas.cost_if_wrong: All-or-nothing over K=3 rejects merges that a greedy walk would have accepted at K=2, so we systematically capture less of the averaging gain than the boss. Worse, _perform_wsm_merge has no time budget and fires in on_train_end, i.e. immediately after our deadline stop, competing for the same 3-minute reserve as the NaN scan, dev absorption and the architecture restore (delta 10). This tournament's diff report names this exact construct: section 3 'Multi-Pass Training with Averaging (MEDIUM CONFIDENCE: risky complexity)' and Do-NOT-port item 3, 'Adds complexity without proven benefit ... implement behind a feature flag and measure win rate before making it default'.
deltas.recommendation: Do not delete averaging - the boss ships more of it than we do and retained the title. Replace our one-shot equal-weight merge with the boss's greedy accept-if-better loop (BOSS 261-332), which is strictly dominant, and add its time bound. Failing that, at minimum add a remaining-time check at the top of _perform_wsm_merge (1044) so it cannot eat the post-training window.

deltas.title: The deadline reserve is a hardcoded 3 minutes on our side and a measured quantity on the boss's
deltas.what: Both start from save_before_remaining_time = 3. The boss then estimates its dev-pass cost from the measured t_per_step and moves the trigger earlier by min(15, max(2, secs/60)) minutes, and re-checks the window before starting the pass at all. Ours uses the bare 3 verbatim - and we have MORE post-training work than the boss (NaN scan + dev absorption + architecture restore) to fit in it.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/customized_trainer.py:1673-1694 (handler uses the value verbatim); set to a literal 3 at /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/instruct_config.py:425, /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/adaptive_config.py:2728, /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/dpo_config.py:249. No site ever adjusts it.

Overrunning it means the container is killed after the deadline eval but before the architecture restore, which by our own comment (customized_trainer.py:583-590) risks the submission, not just its rank.

deltas.title: Live divergence detector: on by default, fires off the step-5 loss, boss has nothing
deltas.what: An on_log hook captures the FIRST logged training loss as init_loss and force-stops the run when any later loss exceeds 3x it after step 50. At logging_steps=5 that baseline is the loss at step 5 - the noisiest, highest point of the run. It is enabled by default (env default '1') and its fire path sets should_evaluate + should_save + should_training_stop. The boss has no divergence detection anywhere in this file.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/customized_trainer.py:227-243 (config, default on at :228), :641-685 (init_loss captured from the first log at :654-655; fire at :668-682). logging_steps=5 at /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/instruct_config.py:231.
deltas.theirs: ABSENT - BOSS/scripts/customized_trainer.py has no on_log hook at all. The boss's only early stop is overfit-based on DEV loss (best*1.05, patience 3, DDP-synced) at BOSS/scripts/checkpoint_avg_callback.py:675-698.
deltas.cost_if_wrong: A single loss spike after step 50 ends the run early. Because the stop also sets should_save, it will not lose the submission, but it truncates training on what may be a healthy run - and the baseline it compares against is the least representative loss of the whole run. (The code and the default are MEASURED at the lines above; the trigger sensitivity is INFERRED - I did not observe it firing on a real run.)
deltas.recommendation: Anchor init_loss on a median of the first N logs rather than log[0] (:654-655), or flip the default to off. Better: replace it with the boss's dev-loss overfit stop, which measures the thing we are ranked on instead of a training-loss ratio.

deltas.title: Early-stop machinery: ~120 lines, half of it dead by default, boss has none in this callback
deltas.what: Adaptive patience derived from a formula, window smoothing over eval history, plus a CV-of-training-loss override. The CV path is env-gated off by default, so ~40 lines of it never execute - yet train_loss_history is still appended on every single log call and grows unbounded for the life of the run. The boss's CustomEvalSaveCallback contains no early stopping at all; its stop lives in the averaging callback and triggers on dev loss so the dev-pass still gets its window.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/customized_trainer.py:161-218 (config; adaptive patience formula at :191-196; CV off by default at :214), :633-639 (unconditional append to train_loss_history), :803-877 (patience + window smoothing + CV override at :822-837)
deltas.theirs: ABSENT from BOSS/scripts/customized_trainer.py entirely. The boss's equivalent is BOSS/scripts/checkpoint_avg_callback.py:675-698 - best_loss*1.05, patience 3, DDP-synced, stops so the dev-pass runs.
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Low direct cost - the stop paths are conservative and always leave the best checkpoint in place. The cost is surface area: the patience formula at 191-196 is opaque (two different derivations, the first overwritten), and dead-by-default code makes the live behaviour hard to reason about under time pressure.
deltas.recommendation: Delete the CV block (:204-218, :817-837) and the unconditional train_loss_history append (:635-639) since nothing else reads it. Keep window smoothing - it is cheap and the non-monotone-cosine motivation is sound - but replace the derived patience with a constant.

deltas.title: save_total_limit 3 (ours) vs unlimited (boss)
deltas.what: We cap retained checkpoints at 3; the boss sets no limit anywhere in its repo. With --save_strategy epoch and our callback pairing eval and save at the same step, promotion always copies the current step, so the cap does not break the copy today. But it removes any possibility of recovering an older checkpoint, and it is the reason our WSM pool has to make its own disk copies (delta 8) where the boss's disk-averaging path can just read the checkpoints that are still there.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/instruct_config.py:229 '--save_total_limit 3'
deltas.theirs: ABSENT - repo-wide grep for save_total_limit over the boss checkout returns nothing; BOSS/scripts/instruct_config.py:155-173 has no such flag. The boss reads back consolidated checkpoints from disk at BOSS/scripts/checkpoint_avg_callback.py:411-455.
deltas.cost_if_wrong: No live defect found. It does foreclose the boss's disk-averaging strategy and forces our pool to duplicate checkpoints we already had on disk.
deltas.recommendation: Keep the cap if disk is genuinely tight, but raise it to at least the WSM K so the pool can reference existing checkpoint dirs instead of copytree-ing its own. If disk is not tight, drop it and match the boss.

The boss subscripts raw (my_state['train']['start_time'], min([...]) over an unchecked list). We extracted two helpers that return None / +inf instead. Our exposure is genuinely larger because our state lives in Redis (a network dependency) while the boss's is a local JSON file.

deltas.cost_if_wrong: Reverting would reintroduce three raise paths in a per-step hook on a Redis-backed state. Cheap insurance, no runtime cost, no effect on selection.

deltas.title: Deadline stop plus the finish-state transition
deltas.what: Both sides stop training at the end_time save so the post-training work can run. Ours additionally forces the shared state to 'finish' when a probe run is preempted by the deadline, because the outer relaunch loop otherwise never sees the transition. The boss's comment at 218-224 records the same reasoning for the stop itself but has no state transition, because its probe path differs.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/customized_trainer.py:574-599 (stop, with the reasoning at 575-593) and :601-629 (finish-state transition, motivated by a measured 244-launch / 700GB incident)

deltas.cost_if_wrong: Reverting the transition reopens a measured runaway-relaunch failure. The stop itself is present on both sides and must stay.

deltas.title: Held-out scoring for LR probes
deltas.what: The multi-run LR sweep picks the probe with the lowest score. The boss scores probes on TRAINING loss. We added probe_eval_fn so probes are scored on held-out loss instead - the metric the validator actually ranks. This is the correct direction and is wired on both instruct and DPO.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/customized_trainer.py:365-407 (_probe_loss, fail-open to train loss), used at :486 and :504; wired at /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/train_instruct.py:655-662 and /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/train_dpo.py:424

deltas.cost_if_wrong: Reverting would put LR selection back on the one signal that rewards fitting the training set harder, which on DPO actively prefers the most destructive LR. Worth noting for calibration though: the boss does this the 'wrong' way and retained the title, so the size of the win here is unproven.

deltas.title: MAX_TRIES lowered 9 -> 3
deltas.what: Each additional try relaunches the trainer as a fresh OS process and repays model load, dataset load and packing for ~80 discarded steps. We capped the ladder at 3; the boss allows 9.

deltas.title: Dev reclaim lives outside the killable path, and nothing reserves time for it
deltas.what: Boss runs its dev reclaim INSIDE the training child, between trainer.train() and success.txt, and widens the training stop trigger by 2-15 minutes sized from the measured per-step cost so the pass has room. We run ours in the orchestrator after run_training() returns, inside the same unmodified 3-minute window that also has to hold two weight scans and the architecture restore. On the gemma run run_training() never returned, so our block never executed; the boss's arrangement executes before the child exits and trains less in order to afford it.
deltas.ours: scripts/text_trainer.py:1350-1388 (gate + absorb_dev_split call, after run_training at :1261); scripts/instruct_config.py:425 sets save_before_remaining_time=3 and no code path raises it (grep over scripts/ finds only :425, adaptive_config.py:2728, dpo_config.py:249, grpo_config.py:332/338)
deltas.theirs: scripts/train_instruct.py:874-899 (dev pass, after trainer.train() at :847, before success.txt at :908-911) and scripts/train_instruct.py:813-830 which sets when_to_eval_handler.save_before_remaining_time = train_request value + _extra_min (2-15 min, from _dev_pass_secs)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: The entire dev-reclaim gain (the boss's own telemetry claimed +0.0183; our own H100 measurement was -0.0194 in loss) is forfeited on every task whose child is pre-empted, which is the normal case at the deadline. On our three round-1 tasks it produced nothing. The gemma gap to rank 1 was 0.0072 — smaller than the mechanism.
deltas.recommendation: Port the boss's placement, not just the mechanism: move the reclaim into train_instruct.py immediately after trainer.train(), reusing the live trainer, and port the save_before_remaining_time widening at train_instruct.py:813-830. Keep our measured rate (r=0.1) rather than the boss's 0.25 — that number is ours, twice measured.

deltas.title: No architecture patch at checkpoint-copy time; the one step that must survive runs last
deltas.what: Boss patches the submission's config.json architectures inside the callback on EVERY submission copy, and treats the orchestrator call as a redundant safety net (its own comment says so). We have no callback-time patch at all — our only patch is the very last thing in main(), after the two scans and the absorption pass. Our own customized_trainer comment already names this exact risk and chose a scheduling fix (stop at the deadline) instead of an architectural one.
deltas.ours: scripts/text_trainer.py:1402 restore_submission_architectures — the sole call; scripts/customized_trainer.py:583-591 documents the hazard but never patches; grep for '_patch_submission_architectures' in scripts/customized_trainer.py returns nothing
deltas.theirs: scripts/customized_trainer.py:78-95 _patch_submission_architectures, called at :319 (save_only path) and :344 (best-checkpoint path); scripts/text_trainer.py:552-555 explicitly labelled 'Final safety net … the primary patch runs on every checkpoint copy'
deltas.cost_if_wrong: A container killed at hours_to_complete ships a config whose architectures the validator's is_finetune check compares verbatim. That is not a few ranks, it is the whole entry — and we have already measured a run finishing 29 seconds PAST its own end_time on our cheapest task.
deltas.recommendation: Port _patch_submission_architectures into our CustomEvalSaveCallback and call it at both copy sites. Keep text_trainer.py:1402 as the net it should have been all along.

deltas.title: The multi-launch LR ladder the boss deleted, and both diff reports condemned
deltas.what: Boss makes exactly ONE call to run_training and says in a comment that multi-restart LR search was removed in favour of in-process refinement inside train_instruct.py. We still relaunch the whole trainer through a state machine, now with lr_search.confirmation_candidates and a GP-EI Bayesian override layered on top, up to 8 launches each with 5 internal retries.
deltas.ours: scripts/text_trainer.py:1127 (while True) through :1310; ladder build at :1160-1194; BO/GP-EI override at :1199-1224; MAX_LOOP_RUNS=8 at :756; runaway guard at :1287-1296 written after a measured 244-launch, 700 GB incident
deltas.theirs: scripts/text_trainer.py:487-489 comment, :500-524 — one run_output_dir, one set_state, one run_training call; scripts/train_instruct.py:16 and :599 run_lr_search in-process instead
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Every extra launch is a full model reload plus a fresh multi-GB output dir, paid from the training budget — the exact budget the boss spends on the dev pass and on more epochs. The 2026-08-31 diff report ranked LES/ladder as the challenger's #1 losing delta; this tournament's report ranks orchestrator complexity #6. Two consecutive validator verdicts against the construct we still carry.
deltas.recommendation: Collapse to a single launch and move LR refinement in-process, as the boss did. If the ladder must stay, gate it behind an env flag defaulting OFF and measure one A/B against the single-run path before a tournament, not during one.

deltas.title: dev_absorption leaves a stale model.safetensors.index.json in the staged submission
deltas.what: Both sides stage a new submission, delete the old weight files, save fresh weights, then swap. The boss's weight-file predicate explicitly includes the shard index; ours does not, so a stale index survives into the staged directory.
deltas.ours: scripts/dev_absorption.py:79-80 _weights_only returns True only for .safetensors/.bin, used at :265 to choose what to delete from staging
deltas.theirs: scripts/dev_pass.py:154-157 _is_weight_file includes the literal 'model.safetensors.index.json' alongside .safetensors and .bin
deltas.cost_if_wrong: If the pre-absorption submission was sharded and save_pretrained writes a single unsharded model.safetensors, the surviving index.json points at shard files we deleted and the submission will not load — a zero, not a worse rank. Triggers exactly on the large models (Qwen3-32B, the 35-71B boss-round task) where a zero is most expensive.
deltas.recommendation: One-line fix: add `or name == "model.safetensors.index.json"` to _weights_only. Cheapest item in this whole diff.

deltas.title: Four post-training stages share a 3-minute window the boss reserves for one
deltas.what: Boss's orchestrator tail is two cheap operations: a config.json edit and a symlink walk. Ours is a NaN/Inf scan over up to 3 shards x 50 tensors, a degenerate-weight scan, a full model reload plus a training pass over the dev split, a possible base-model clone, and only then the architecture restore — all inside the same untouched three minutes.
deltas.ours: scripts/text_trainer.py:1322 checkpoint_has_nan_or_inf, :1325-1326 checkpoint_weights_are_degenerate, :1350-1388 dev absorption, :1391-1397 noise fallback, :1402 restore_submission_architectures; the StageClock at :1117 exists precisely because this window was already measured to overrun
deltas.theirs: scripts/text_trainer.py:555 patch_submission_config, :557 patch_wandb_symlinks — nothing else after run_training returns
deltas.cost_if_wrong: The ordering puts the only entry-critical step (architecture restore) LAST, behind an optional expensive one (absorption). Any overrun kills the step whose absence voids the submission and preserves the steps whose absence costs nothing.
deltas.recommendation: Reorder immediately even before the bigger move: run restore_submission_architectures FIRST, right after the child returns, then the scans, then absorption. Ideally combine with porting the callback-time patch so ordering stops mattering.

deltas.title: add_random_noise: our fallback works on models the boss's cannot load
deltas.what: Boss's fallback builds the model with AutoModelForCausalLM and re-saves it. Ours imports no transformers at all — it clones the base directory (hardlinked where possible, un-linking only the shard it edits) and perturbs one tensor on disk.
deltas.ours: scripts/add_random_noise.py:54-74 _clone_tree, :77-90 _break_link, :105-142 _perturb_safetensors, :145-180 main
deltas.theirs: scripts/add_random_noise.py:14 AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_path, …), :29-30 model.save_pretrained / tokenizer.save_pretrained
deltas.cost_if_wrong: On any 2026-pool model (qwen3_5, gemma4, lfm2, lfm2_moe — 9 of 12 entries under transformers 4.51.3) the boss's fallback raises, submission_dir stays empty and the upload creates no repo at all. Ours still ships something. This is the difference between last place and no entry on task 29fc1a10.
deltas.recommendation: Keep unchanged. This is one of the few places we are strictly ahead of the retained champion, and it is a forfeit-class difference.

deltas.title: Both sides still noise the embeddings on the fallback path, at the same std
deltas.what: NOISE_STD is 0.01 on both sides and both perturb the input embeddings. Our own module docstring argues the validator's model_is_a_finetune compares CONFIG ATTRIBUTES ONLY and that a verbatim copy satisfies it — then keeps the perturbation anyway 'to preserve the original intent'.
deltas.ours: scripts/add_random_noise.py:35 NOISE_STD = 0.01, applied at :136-137; the reasoning that makes it unnecessary is at :19-26
deltas.theirs: scripts/add_random_noise.py:17 noise_std = 0.01, applied at :22-24 — identical value, identical target tensor
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Our noised base scored 3.2921 against another miner's un-noised base at 2.8929 on the same task — roughly 0.4 nats thrown away on a task we had already lost the training half of. On a bracket that orders on MEAN per-task rank, a forfeited task's score still moves the mean.
deltas.recommendation: Set NOISE_STD to 0 (or gate the perturbation behind an env flag defaulting off) and ship the clean clone. Our own file already argues the copy passes the check. This is a free rank on every forfeit, and the boss has the same problem so it is not a divergence risk.

deltas.title: Preflight forfeit path: we divert unloadable models, the boss burns eight retries
deltas.what: We detect an architecture transformers cannot build and a tokenisation step that produced nothing, and skip straight to the fallback. The boss has neither check — it runs the full retry budget against a model that can never load, then noises.
deltas.ours: scripts/text_trainer.py:256-296 detect_unloadable_architecture (deliberately narrowed to the single 'does not recognize this architecture' marker so a half-downloaded snapshot is NOT diverted), :875-880 the load_blocker, :177-241 tokenisation_gate, :1105-1110 the gate wiring, :1128-1129 the loop short-circuit
deltas.theirs: ABSENT — scripts/text_trainer.py:353 retries default 8, :183 the loop, no config preflight and no tokenisation gate anywhere in scripts/
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Without it an lfm2 task spends its whole budget on 8 identical failing loads and reaches the fallback with the clock gone. With the boss's un-loadable fallback on top, that is a zero.
deltas.recommendation: Keep. Note it is only worth its complexity because of the paired add_random_noise rewrite — the two are one mechanism and should be reviewed together.

deltas.title: quiet_mode: the boss publishes nothing to the shared logs, we publish our whole strategy
deltas.what: Boss imports a quiet gate as the very first import in all eight process entrypoints; it no-ops print() to stdout, forces library log levels to ERROR and kills tqdm, on by default, preserving stderr and tracebacks. We have no equivalent — grep for SN56_QUIET/quiet_mode/TQDM_DISABLE over scripts/ and dockerfiles/ returns nothing.
deltas.ours: ABSENT (no quiet gate anywhere); the leaked lines are e.g. scripts/text_trainer.py:1092-1098 [CONFIG-RESOLVED] path/lr/batch/steps/model, :1170-1172 the LR candidate list, :1218-1221 the BO override, :1388 the stage clock, plus [dev-absorb] and [FAST-CRASH] markers
deltas.theirs: scripts/quiet_mode.py:1-139; imported first at scripts/text_trainer.py:6, add_random_noise.py:1, train_instruct.py, train_dpo.py, train_grpo.py, tokenize_instruct.py, tokenize_dpo.py, tokenize_grpo.py
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Our training logs ship to Grafana Loki and are public. Our own recon skill mines rival miners' Loki logs; every rival can mine ours. We are broadcasting the adaptive-vs-legacy decision, the exact LR, batch, step count and model, and the name of every mechanism we run.
deltas.recommendation: Port quiet_mode.py essentially verbatim. IMPORTANT PAIRED CHANGE: the boss also rewrote run_cmd_with_log's forwarding from print() to sys.stdout.write (their text_trainer.py:70-78) precisely because print is shimmed — ours still uses print at scripts/text_trainer.py:69, so porting quiet_mode without that change would silence the child log stream and break get_error_type's OOM detection.

deltas.title: State channel: a redis daemon with a silent process-local fallback vs a JSON file
deltas.what: Boss's state_manager is 20 lines writing /tmp/trainer_state.json. Ours is 80 lines over redis, with an in-memory fallback when the module or the connection is unavailable — and that fallback is PROCESS-LOCAL, so it does not carry anything between the orchestrator and the training child.
deltas.ours: scripts/state_manager.py:10-19 (optional import, _FALLBACK_STATE), :42-43 and :53-56 (get falls back to a process-local dict), :62-63 and :69-71 (set does the same); scripts/entrypoint.sh starts redis-server and tolerates failure; consumers that need the cross-process channel: scripts/train_instruct.py:885-888 (lrrt_lr), scripts/customized_trainer.py:786-791 (best checkpoint)
deltas.theirs: scripts/state_manager.py:1-20 — STATE_FILE = '/tmp/trainer_state.json', get_state/set_state, no dependency, no daemon, no fallback needed
deltas.cost_if_wrong: If redis-server does not come up in the container, every cross-process write is silently dropped: text_trainer's ladder never sees lrrt_lr and falls open to the ladder we know picks badly, and customized_trainer's cross-run best-checkpoint memory is lost. The failure prints one line and otherwise looks identical to a healthy run.
deltas.recommendation: Replace the redis backend with the boss's file. It removes a package pin (training_requirements.txt redis==7.0.1), an apt package, an entrypoint daemon and a two-second sleep, and it cannot degrade to a silently wrong answer. This is exactly the simplification the diff reports keep asking for.

deltas.title: Absorption hyperparameters diverge from the boss's on every axis, and batch_size=1 is not one of our measured choices
deltas.what: Boss matches the dev pass to training on purpose: effective batch equals training's (accum computed from train per-device x grad-accum), LR is the run's own scheduler floor, weight_decay 0.0 on trainable params only, training's max_grad_norm, and the trainer's own training_step so the loss is right for the task type. Ours reloads the model from disk and runs batch_size=1 with no accumulation — one optimizer step per row — AdamW over all parameters at default weight_decay, clip hardcoded to 1.0, plain causal-LM loss.
deltas.ours: scripts/dev_absorption.py:130 batch_size=1 default and :193 DataLoader(batch_size=batch_size) with no accumulation; :194 AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=lr) (weight_decay defaults to 0.01); :221 clip_grad_norm_(…, 1.0); :219 plain forward; :171-173 AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(submission_dir); rate at :53 DEFAULT_MIN_LR_RATE=0.1
deltas.theirs: scripts/dev_pass.py:90 accum = round(train_per_device * train_grad_accum / per_device_eval) with the explicit rationale at :17-20; :83 AdamW(trainable, lr=min_lr, weight_decay=0.0); :129-130 accelerator.clip_grad_norm_(…, max_grad_norm); :127 trainer.training_step; :64 reuses trainer.model_wrapped; rate from the run's own lr_scheduler_kwargs at scripts/train_instruct.py:876-887
deltas.cost_if_wrong: batch_size=1 makes each step a far noisier, effectively hotter update than either calibration assumes — the boss's whole argument at dev_pass.py:17-20 is that an unsharded small batch makes min_lr effectively too hot with no eval left to catch the damage. Our r=0.1 was measured at whatever batch our A/B used, so the rate and the batch are not independently validated.
deltas.recommendation: Keep our measured r=0.1 (two independent measurements back it). Change the batch: add gradient accumulation so the effective batch matches training, exactly as dev_pass.py:90 does, and set weight_decay=0.0. Re-run the r sweep once after that, because changing the batch invalidates the rate calibration.

deltas.title: Our absorption has a hotness guard the boss's does not
deltas.what: We refuse to swap in the absorbed weights when the pass's mean loss exceeds the checkpoint's own recorded dev loss, reading the number checkpoint selection itself wrote and distinguishing the train-loss-proxy loss.txt format from the real one. The boss has no such check — its only protection is the exception wrapper and the atomic swap.
deltas.ours: scripts/dev_absorption.py:83-122 _prior_dev_loss (incl. the proxy= discrimination at :106-108) and :248-256 the refusal
deltas.theirs: ABSENT — scripts/dev_pass.py has no loss comparison anywhere; the only guards are :68-71 (no trainable params), :100-102 (empty loader) and the caller's try/except at scripts/train_instruct.py:905-906
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Dropping it would remove the only thing standing between a mis-calibrated absorption LR and a silently degraded submission, on a pass that by construction has no held-out data left. Our own 28c9f3bb measurement showed the two harmful rates averaging 1.8664 and 2.6956 against a prior of 1.7893 — the guard separates them cleanly.
deltas.recommendation: Keep, and carry it across when the mechanism moves into the child. Reading loss.txt works there too (the callback writes it before trainer.train() returns).

deltas.title: utility.py: we deleted three helpers the boss actively uses
deltas.what: We removed smart_truncate, apply_prompt_loss_weight and gaussian_subsample and replaced the first with a tail-slice inside pad_sequence. All three are live in the boss, not dead code.
deltas.ours: scripts/utility.py:45-58 pad_sequence with `sequence = sequence[-max_length:]`; smart_truncate, apply_prompt_loss_weight and gaussian_subsample absent from the file; scripts/train_instruct.py has no plw or subsample call (grep returns nothing)
deltas.theirs: scripts/utility.py:45-80 smart_truncate wired into pad_inputs at :157; :83-112 apply_prompt_loss_weight called at scripts/train_instruct.py:279-280 when prompt:completion > 5:1; :115-149 gaussian_subsample called at scripts/train_instruct.py:702-715 when measured coverage < 0.5 on >2000 rows
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Two live training features we do not have at all (prompt-loss-weight for prompt-dominated data, difficulty-weighted subsampling when the budget cannot cover an epoch). Plus a semantic change: when the completion alone exceeds max_length, the boss keeps the START of the answer (utility.py:68-71) while our tail-slice keeps the END with no beginning.
deltas.recommendation: Both features are gated on baseline_stats/measured coverage, which we do not currently pass to the child (see the next delta) — fix that first, then port apply_prompt_loss_weight and gaussian_subsample behind their own gates. Restore smart_truncate's completion-overflow branch, or at least decide our tail-slice deliberately rather than by deletion.

deltas.title: baseline_stats never reaches the training child
deltas.what: Boss accepts baseline stats on the CLI, from an env var or from a file path, and threads the parsed dict into train_info so the child reads it out of the request JSON. We read the same env var only in the parent's adaptive_config, and never put it in train_info, so the child cannot see it.
deltas.ours: scripts/text_trainer.py:759-813 — no --baseline-stats argument; train_info at :884-908 has no 'baseline_stats' key; the only reader is scripts/adaptive_config.py:1099-1114 via baseline_stats_reader.read_cached(), in the orchestrator process
deltas.theirs: scripts/text_trainer.py:358-366 the CLI arg, :372-384 the CLI/env/file parse, :454 '"baseline_stats": baseline_stats' inside train_info; consumed in the child at scripts/train_instruct.py:272-281
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Every child-side use of validator-provided statistics is unavailable to us by construction — this is the wiring that makes the boss's PLW and subsample gates possible. It is a disconnected-wire, not a missing algorithm.
deltas.recommendation: Add 'baseline_stats' to train_info at scripts/text_trainer.py:884-908, reading it the way the boss does (CLI arg + BASELINE_STATS_PATH + BASELINE_STATS, our baseline_stats_reader already implements the env half). Cheap, and it unblocks two other ports.

deltas.title: Tokenizer sanitisation: ours covers the step the boss's does not, but drops tokens the boss preserves
deltas.what: Both repos independently fixed the same anonymised-model bug (extra_special_tokens serialised as a list). Boss repairs it list-to-dict inside a load_tokenizer wrapper used at the three train_* entrypoints. We repair it once on disk in the orchestrator, before the tokenisation subprocess, by REMOVING the field and relying on tokenizer.json.
deltas.ours: scripts/text_trainer.py:856-857 maybe_sanitize_for_anon_model(model_path), before the tokenize subprocess at :1104; scripts/tokenizer_sanitizer.py:1-141 (also strips placeholder tokenizer_class values)
deltas.theirs: scripts/model_utility.py fix_tokenizer_config + load_tokenizer (list-to-dict repair), called at scripts/train_instruct.py:223-224, train_dpo.py:147-148, train_grpo.py:331-332; but scripts/tokenize_instruct.py:284 calls bare AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained and is NOT covered
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Ours covers a step the boss leaves exposed (the axolotl-venv tokenisation), which is worth keeping. But field removal is lossier than list-to-dict conversion: if tokenizer.json does not carry equivalent added_tokens for some family, we lose special tokens the boss keeps.
deltas.recommendation: Keep our placement (orchestrator, pre-tokenisation, on disk) and adopt the boss's repair semantics: convert list-to-dict rather than deleting the field, falling back to deletion only when the entries are not convertible.

deltas.title: Lost the FlashAttention head-size guard on vLLM selection
deltas.what: Boss disables vLLM when the model's attention head size is not one FlashAttention supports, computed from the config. Our model_utility.py is the older upstream plus our anonymisation-safe fingerprint work, and never gained that check.
deltas.ours: scripts/model_utility.py get_use_vllm — fingerprint blocklist plus the legacy name list, no head-size computation anywhere in the file
deltas.theirs: scripts/model_utility.py _FLASH_ATTN_HEAD_SIZES + _has_compatible_head_size, called from get_use_vllm before returning True (visible in the diff of the two files: our version deletes both)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: GRPO tasks only. A model with an unsupported head size gets vLLM enabled, crashes, and recovers only through the OOM/VLLM retry ladder — burning attempts on a failure the config could have predicted for free.
deltas.recommendation: Port _has_compatible_head_size and call it from get_use_vllm. It is ~15 lines and reads the config we already load.

deltas.title: OOM ladder floors: max_length 512 and 5 retries vs 2048 and 8
deltas.what: Same ladder shape on both sides (halve batch, then halve max_length in the request JSON, then for GRPO disable vLLM), different floors and different retry budgets.
deltas.ours: scripts/text_trainer.py:331 MIN_OOM_MAX_LENGTH = 512, applied in halve_request_max_length at :334-376; :799 --retries default 5
deltas.theirs: scripts/text_trainer.py:222 `new_maxlen = max(2048, cur_maxlen // 2)` — floor hardcoded at 2048; :353 --retries default 8
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Our floor lets an OOM ladder train on 512-token rows for a task whose p95 is 2675 — a submission that completes but has seen a truncated fraction of every long row, which is precisely the failure mode we already measured once (490 of 27992 rows trained). The boss refuses to go below 2048 and accepts the OOM instead. Our lower retry count also gives the ladder three fewer rungs.
deltas.recommendation: Raise MIN_OOM_MAX_LENGTH to 1024 or 2048 and take --retries back to 8. If 512 is deliberate, log loudly at that rung so the gauge cannot report health while the run is starved.

deltas.title: DEV_ABSORPTION comment says 'Default OFF'; the code defaults ON
deltas.what: The block's own justification argues the mechanism stays gated until we measure it on our own harness, and states it is default OFF. The getenv default is '1'.
deltas.ours: scripts/text_trainer.py:1345 'Default OFF. …' against :1350 `os.getenv("DEV_ABSORPTION", "1") == "1"` — identical in the commit that ran, git show 12b16b5:scripts/text_trainer.py:1351
deltas.theirs: N/A — the boss's gate is structural, not env-driven: scripts/train_instruct.py:874 `is_final_run and _avg_mode == "ram" and _dev_n > 0 and _dev_window_ok`
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Documentation defect, not a runtime one — but it is the kind that makes a post-mortem read the wrong story. Anyone auditing why we produced no absorption telemetry would conclude the feature was off, when in fact it was armed and starved of time.
deltas.recommendation: Fix the comment to match the code (it is armed), or flip the default and say so. Then adopt the boss's structural gate instead of an env flag.

deltas.title: is_openai / transformers upgrade path is byte-identical on both sides
deltas.what: Both call the same three pip commands in a subprocess when the architecture is GptOssForCausalLM, and neither re-imports transformers in the parent. Ours additionally documents why gpt_oss is deliberately excluded from our unloadable-architecture preflight.
deltas.ours: scripts/text_trainer.py:861-876 (pip transformers==4.55.0, deepspeed==0.17.4, kernels==0.9.0), :298-302 is_openai_model, :928-932 the gpt_oss preflight exclusion comment
deltas.theirs: scripts/text_trainer.py:415-431 — same three commands, same pins; :145-149 is_openai_model, identical body
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Nothing. Neither side guards anything the other does not on this path; the parent's already-imported transformers stays stale in both, and the child gets the upgraded one because it is a fresh interpreter.
deltas.recommendation: Leave alone. The only asymmetry is our extra preflight-exclusion comment, which is correct and costs nothing.

deltas.title: StageClock and FAST-CRASH telemetry: cheap, control-flow-free, boss-absent
deltas.what: We time and label every stage between the training deadline and the finished submission, and tag any training attempt that exits in under 60 seconds. The boss has neither.
deltas.ours: scripts/text_trainer.py:80-124 StageClock, marks at :1261, :1264, :1327, :1388, :1400; :465-476 the [FAST-CRASH] marker
deltas.theirs: ABSENT — no stage timing and no fast-crash detection anywhere in scripts/text_trainer.py
deltas.cost_if_wrong: These cost nothing at runtime, never raise and never alter control flow — and the FAST-CRASH marker is what identified the TRL-import failure that noised all three runs in tourn_e758aac2d861c378_20260824. Removing them would blind the exact window we now know we overrun.
deltas.recommendation: Keep — but route them to stderr, not stdout, before porting quiet_mode. Otherwise they either leak to Loki or get silenced along with everything else.

deltas.title: The champion's 'devfit,absorb=' telemetry is not in THIS boss revision
deltas.what: Our dev_absorption module was built to match a loss.txt string we observed on an earlier champion snapshot. Grep for 'absorb' (case-insensitive) over the entire retained-boss repo returns zero hits; its loss.txt formats are '<step>,<loss>', '<step>,no_eval' and 'disk_avg,<metric>'.
deltas.ours: scripts/dev_absorption.py:11-13 cites `devfit,absorb=+0.0183` as the provenance of the whole module
deltas.theirs: ABSENT — scripts/customized_trainer.py:322-324 and :347-349 and scripts/checkpoint_avg_callback.py:462-463 are the only loss.txt writers, and none of them emits an absorb= field; scripts/dev_pass.py:182-186 deliberately PRESERVES whatever loss.txt already says
deltas.cost_if_wrong: None directly, but it corrects the framing: the champion did not lose the mechanism, it stopped publishing the telemetry. Comparing our trigger conditions against a string is comparing against nothing; the real comparison is against dev_pass.py, and that is delta #1.
deltas.recommendation: Update dev_absorption.py's provenance comment to point at scripts/dev_pass.py in this repo rather than at a telemetry string, so the next reader compares mechanism to mechanism.

deltas.title: HF eval/save cadence is never switched on — the gemma run produced exactly 2 evals

We never assign eval_strategy or eval_steps ANYWHERE — `grep -n 'eval_strategy|eval_steps' customized_trainer.py text_trainer.py train_instruct.py` returns zero hits on our side and 12 on the boss's. So `--eval_strategy no` (instruct_config.py:227) stands for the whole run and the ONLY evals are the ones CustomEvalSaveCallback forces: periodic_save_steps=500 and the end_time save. MEASURED in the tournament log: the entire gemma run logged two eval_loss lines, at epoch 0.69 (step ~500, 0.0527852) and epoch 0.75 (step ~544, 0.0517329). The boss's cadence on the same shape of run is ~8-10.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/instruct_config.py:227 (`--eval_strategy no`), and the proven absence of any override in /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/train_instruct.py (no `training_args.eval_strategy` assignment anywhere in the file)

The already-known 349.7s telemetry bug picked the wrong one of those two (0.0527852 shipped instead of 0.0517329, a 0.0010 gap on a task we lost by 0.0072). With the boss's cadence there would have been ~8 candidates spread across the run and an overfit signal early enough to act on. This is also the precondition for any checkpoint averaging: you cannot soup a window of 3 when only 2 snapshots exist.
deltas.recommendation: Port boss train_instruct.py:438-449 verbatim (the is_final_run gate plus the four assignments). It is 12 lines, uses only values we already have (hours_to_complete, total_steps_all_epochs), and needs no new module. Highest value-per-line change in this subsystem.

deltas.title: No time-aware epoch planning — the cosine schedule spans 3x the steps the budget can run
deltas.what: The boss recomputes num_train_epochs from the MEASURED per-step time returned by its LR search: remaining_secs*0.85/t_per_step -> achievable_steps; optimal_epochs = round(max(1.3, min(4.0 if len(train_ds)<10000 else 3.0, 1.25*achievable/steps_per_epoch)), 2), then rewrites num_train_epochs, warmup_steps, eval_steps and save_steps and broadcasts them across ranks. The whole point, in its own comment, is that the cosine finishes at ~94% progress when the timer cuts, i.e. LR is at ~min_lr. We have no equivalent. Our epoch count is a static integer chosen at config time from init_loss (adaptive_config.py:2177 <- dynamics_utils.adaptive_epochs_from_init_loss) and never revisited. MEASURED on gemma: `[adaptive-instruct] ... epoch=3`, `total_steps_per_epoch: 722; total_steps_all_epochs: 2166.0`, `max_steps: -1`, and the run stopped at epoch 0.75 (~544 steps). The cosine had covered 25% of its span, so the LR at submission was still ~88% of peak with min_lr_rate 0.15 — the model was never annealed at all.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/adaptive_config.py:2177 (`"epoch_num": epochs`), and the proven absence of any num_train_epochs reassignment in /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/train_instruct.py
deltas.theirs: scripts/train_instruct.py:726-801
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Every instruct run ships a model stopped mid-decay instead of one whose schedule completed. This is the same failure recorded for 597dc05e on 2026-08-31 and it recurred here. It is a first-order loss-quality effect and it costs on EVERY task, not just this one — the boss's floor of 1.3 epochs and its 1.25 stretch exist precisely to spend the whole budget on a completed schedule.
deltas.recommendation: Port boss train_instruct.py:726-801. It depends on t_per_step, which means it must come with a real in-process measurement (see the LR-search delta below) — a measurement is available for free from the first N training steps even if we do not adopt the whole search. Do NOT try to substitute the EXPT_MAX_STEPS cap for this: capping max_steps truncates the plan, it does not re-fit the schedule to the budget.

deltas.title: LR selection: boss searches in-process and keeps the work; ours sweeps, discards the weights, and proposed 29x below the incumbent
deltas.what: Boss: run_lr_search is called inside train_instruct on the REAL train dataloader at the REAL batch with the real optimizer, budget-planned to at most 20% of the task budget (lr_search.py:139 _SEARCH_FRACTION=0.20), degrading full -> two_stage -> validate -> skip by how many epochs are affordable; every non-skip mode carries the best probe's weights forward (lr_search.py:222-224: "search steps are kept work, not thrown away"); it returns (best_lr, t_per_step), assigns trainer.args.learning_rate = best_lr, and caches best_lr + batch in state so an OOM retry does not repeat it. Ours: a separate LRRT sweep, gated to `checking_mode == "first_time"`, whose FINALLY block mandatorily reloads the model from disk to throw the sweep's weights away, and whose only output is state["lrrt_lr"] read by a DIFFERENT process (text_trainer.py:1161). MEASURED on gemma: the block ran four times (11:23, 11:25, 14:37, 14:39), each ~55s of sweep plus ~60s of reload, and each time logged `[lr-search] reloading model to discard the sweep's weights`. All four returned `lrrt=1.000e-06 (clamped from 5.214e-07) incumbent=2.860e-05 ... UNBRACKETED(nothing above the incumbent)` — 29x below the incumbent, while its own loss-minimum candidate was 1.707e-04, 6x above.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/train_instruct.py:717-916, with the mandatory discard at 894-916 and the state write at 886-888
deltas.theirs: scripts/train_instruct.py:565-654 (search, batch sync, LR cache), scripts/lr_search.py:209-280 (plan_budget), scripts/lr_search.py:92,137,139,144 (constants)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Two costs, both paid. (a) ~7.7 GPU-minutes per task burned on four sweeps whose weights are deliberately destroyed, on a run that then only had time for 0.75 of its planned 3 epochs. (b) No t_per_step measurement exists in our process at all, which is what makes the epoch-planning delta above unfixable in isolation. The picker's answer was also unusable (UNBRACKETED on all four invocations), so the LR actually used came from family_lr_table at 2.86e-05 — already flagged as below every other estimator we have.
deltas.recommendation: Do not patch the LRRT picker. Replace the whole block with boss lr_search.run_lr_search called at the same site, which gives us a searched LR, a measured t_per_step, weights that are kept, an OOM-halving path, and a cross-attempt LR cache in one move. If that is too large for one change, take the minimum viable piece first: measure t_per_step over the first ~20 real training steps and feed the epoch planner, and delete the LRRT block entirely.

deltas.title: Static vocab-aware batch cap vs the boss's runtime OOM halving — ours cut batch 60->8 and still OOM'd
deltas.what: The boss has NO memory model and NO vocab cap. Its batch is the INSTRUCT_CONFIG bucket (48 for 2-4B), adjusted only by model-family rules and by one max_length compensation (batch *= 2048/max_length when max_length rose above the 2048 default). OOM is handled empirically at two places: `_halve_batch_dataloader` inside the LR search, which halves per_device_train_batch_size and rebuilds the dataloader in-process and carries the survivor into training (with an all_reduce(MIN) so every rank adopts the smallest surviving batch), and the process-level retry ladder in text_trainer.py:188-210. Ours computes a VRAM estimate (estimate_max_batch_size, adaptive_config.py:1308), then a 1-GPU empirical bucket, then a length scaling, then a GQA boost, then a hard vocab cap. MEASURED on gemma-2-2b (vocab 256000): `batch bucket scaled for length: 60 -> 25 (max_length=2424 vs reference 1024)`, `gqa-batch-boost ... 25->27`, then the vocab cap at adaptive_config.py:1497-1509 forced 8 (2e9<=param<5e9 branch), and training STILL hit `torch.OutOfMemoryError ... Tried to allocate 18.49 GiB` and text_trainer halved to 4. Effective batch 16 against the boss table's 48.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/adaptive_config.py:1307-1312, 1414-1425, 1447-1466, 1489-1509
deltas.theirs: scripts/instruct_config.py:38-43 (2_4_b batch 48) and :310-320 (max_length compensation); the proven absence of any vocab or VRAM cap in that file; runtime halving at scripts/train_instruct.py:586-596 and 613-628; process retry at scripts/text_trainer.py:188-210
deltas.cost_if_wrong: The cap did not buy safety — it OOM'd anyway — and it cost a full process restart plus a 3-12x smaller batch than the boss's table on the same model class. Smaller batch at fixed wall clock means fewer samples seen, which is the direct mechanism behind our 0.0072 gap. Four stacked adjustments (VRAM estimate, bucket, length scale, GQA boost, vocab cap) each fitted on a different run also mean no single number can be attributed or corrected.
deltas.recommendation: Delete the vocab cap and the GQA boost, keep one starting batch (the boss's bucket, with the boss's max_length compensation), and adopt the boss's in-search halving so the batch is DISCOVERED once per task instead of predicted five times. Verify against the gemma log: the boss's compensated batch would be 48*2048/2424 = 40, which would halve to 20 or 10 in-process rather than costing a restart.

deltas.title: No dev pass — the champion reclaims the held-out dev split as one low-LR epoch and we do not
deltas.what: After trainer.train() the boss runs one epoch over the dev split at lr = learning_rate * min_lr_rate (0.25 by default, read back out of lr_scheduler_kwargs), from the best checkpoint, then does a weights-only atomic swap into submission_dir, guarded by a window check that skips a pass that cannot finish. It also moves the end-time stop earlier by the pass's estimated cost so the window exists at all. We do nothing after trainer.train() except write success.txt.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/train_instruct.py:919-926 (trainer.train() then success.txt, nothing between)
deltas.theirs: scripts/train_instruct.py:803-829 (budgeting) and 848-908 (the pass), plus scripts/dev_pass.py:45-194
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Our own measurement (memory: dev absorption) puts this at -0.0194 on one task and -0.0052 on a second, against a top-three spread smaller than either. On gemma our gap to rank 1 was 0.0072. This single missing block is larger than the gap. MEASURED: our gemma log contains zero occurrences of 'devfit' or 'absorb'; the champion publishes 'devfit,absorb=' in loss.txt on every task.
deltas.recommendation: Port dev_pass.py and both boss blocks. It is the highest-confidence positive-delta port available: we have already measured the effect twice at the default rate and know the cliff is above r=0.2. Note it depends on the end-time trigger actually STOPPING training (boss CustomEvalSaveCallback) — our equivalent stop exists at customized_trainer.py:574+, so the window is obtainable.

deltas.what: Boss registers AdaptiveTrainingCallback(window=3, averaging_mode=ram|disk) on every final run, choosing RAM averaging for non-sharded models that fit host RAM and disk averaging for FSDP/DeepSpeed or when 6x trainable bytes exceeds 100GB, and bounds the greedy soup's eval time by end_time. checkpoint_avg_callback.py is 34,954 bytes — the boss's single largest addition. We register only CustomEvalSaveCallback plus two env-gated observability callbacks.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/train_instruct.py:512-551 (callbacks_list — CustomEvalSaveCallback, MetricsCallback, ExperimentLoggerCallback only)
deltas.theirs: scripts/train_instruct.py:14 (import), 484-505 (mode selection and construction), 516-518 (registration)

Our WSM merge gate (train_instruct.py:602-645) is the nearest thing we have and it gates a merge we barely produce.

deltas.title: We leave dev unpacked; the boss packs dev under Flash Attention
deltas.what: Boss packs the dev set with PackedDataset(use_fa=True) when packing_mode == 'fa', and explicitly refuses to pack it under naive packing because cross-sequence attention would corrupt eval loss. We never pack dev, by a deliberate argument: the validator scores a flat mean over EXAMPLES with per_device_eval_batch_size pinned to 1, so a packed dev block turns eval_loss into a token-weighted mean — a different functional from the one we are ranked on.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/train_instruct.py:324-331 (comment) and the absence of any dev PackedDataset call
deltas.theirs: scripts/train_instruct.py:330-346, and scripts/monkeypatch.py:287-302 (PackedDataset use_fa parameter, which our copy at monkeypatch.py:243-253 does not have)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: The correctness argument is right and it is the reason our dev-loss gauge is calibrated at all. But it is not free: MEASURED, our gemma evals cost 109-110s each over 965 unpacked dev examples at batch 1. If we adopt the boss's ~8-10 evals per run, that is 15-18 minutes of eval on a 1.75h budget. Packing dev would cut the block count roughly 2.5x (train packed 25231 -> 11567 at the same length).
deltas.recommendation: Keep dev unpacked for the number we SELECT on, but do not pay 110s per eval to get it — either shrink the dev set used for in-run selection (a fixed 250-row subsample scored the validator's way) or run a cheap packed eval for cadence and one unpacked eval at the deadline. Decide by measuring eval wall-clock as a fraction of budget, not by argument.

deltas.title: We disable packing entirely on non-Flash-Attention models; the boss falls back to naive packing
deltas.what: When disable_fa is True (alibi models like falcon-rw, OPT), we set packing='False' and train unpacked. The boss keeps packing='True' and sets packing_mode='naive', taking the PackedDataset path with use_fa=False, which resets position_ids per sequence instead of relying on FA varlen. Its comment: 'Still much better than no packing (~2-3x throughput from reduced padding).' Our PackedDataset has no use_fa parameter at all, so the fallback is not merely unconfigured — it does not exist in our code.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/instruct_config.py:347-350; /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/monkeypatch.py:243-253 (no use_fa)
deltas.theirs: scripts/instruct_config.py:227-235; scripts/train_instruct.py:309-317; scripts/monkeypatch.py:287-302
deltas.cost_if_wrong: On any alibi/OPT/falcon draw we train on padded batches while the boss trains ~2-3x more tokens per step in the same wall clock. This did not bite on the 2026-09-07 round (all three models were FA-capable) but falcon-rw-1b has already appeared twice in tournaments we entered.
deltas.recommendation: Port the use_fa parameter into monkeypatch.PackedDataset and the packing_mode plumbing. It is a contained change (one parameter, one branch) with a large, mechanically obvious throughput win on a model class we have already drawn.

deltas.title: min_lr_rate is family-varied (gemma got 0.15); the boss uses 0.25 always
deltas.what: The boss hardcodes min_lr_rate 0.25 in run_config and reads it back in the dev pass. We carry a per-family table with values 0.15, 0.20, 0.25 and 0.75 depending on the resolved family. MEASURED: `[adaptive-instruct] family=gemma ... min_lr_rate=0.15`.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/adaptive_config.py:619-620 (gemma profile) and :2180 (`"min_lr_rate": instruct_hp["min_lr_rate"] if instruct_hp else 0.25`)
deltas.theirs: scripts/instruct_config.py:207 (`"min_lr_rate": 0.25`) and :166-167 (template)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: On its own this is second-order — but it compounds with the epoch-planning defect. The boss's whole schedule argument is 'stop at ~94% of a cosine so the LR lands at min_lr'; a lower floor only helps if you REACH it. We stopped at 25% of the schedule, so 0.15 vs 0.25 changed nothing this run and could only hurt once the schedule is fixed. The 0.75 entry is the more alarming one: a near-constant LR is exactly the class of unvalidated scheduler change the diff report condemns.

deltas.title: state["train"] is dereferenced unguarded, and our state lives in Redis while the boss's lives in a file
deltas.what: Boss: `state = get_state(); if "train" not in state: state["train"] = {}` before writing start_train_time, backed by a plain /tmp/trainer_state.json. Ours writes `state["train"]["start_train_time"]` with no guard, backed by Redis; when Redis is unreachable our get_state falls back to a PROCESS-LOCAL dict (state_manager.py:43,56), and train_instruct runs in a subprocess, so it would see {} and raise KeyError before a single step. entrypoint.sh:6 starts redis-server with `|| echo`, so a failure to start is swallowed. The boss deleted redis from training_requirements.txt entirely; we still pin redis==7.0.1.

But the same silent fallback also breaks the lrrt_lr handoff (written in train_instruct, read in text_trainer) and the LR-ladder history, which would degrade to the geometric ladder we measured at 777x off.

deltas.title: TrainingArguments CLI deltas: five flags we add, one the boss adds, one behaviour change
deltas.what: Ours adds, relative to the boss template: --save_total_limit 3, --seed {seed}, --label_smoothing_factor {label_smoothing} (always 0.0), --weight_decay {weight_decay} (variable; boss is a literal 0.), --neftune_noise_alpha {neftune_noise_alpha}, and --ddp_find_unused_parameters True on multi-GPU DDP. Boss adds --dataloader_pin_memory True (HF default is already True, so no-op) and sets neftune in-script instead: always-on alpha=1, escalating to 5 when baseline gradient_noise_scale > 1.0. deltas.title: The boss's in-process trial LR search does not exist on our side at all
deltas.what: BOSS runs 4-16 short REAL training trials at different LRs inside the training process (weights saved/restored, identical cached batches, divergence+relative pruning), then selects edge-of-stability among them and returns both the LR and a measured t_per_step for epoch planning; the trials cost <=20% of wall clock and never restart the run. OURS runs a 100-step LR range test whose only product is a number handed to a separate multi-run orchestration layer. We have no code that trains at a candidate LR and compares losses inside the run.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/lr_search.py:1-183 (whole file is candidate arithmetic; grep for farejando/select_edge_lr/plan_budget/_run_trial/_restore_trainable_state over scripts/ returns zero hits)

deltas.cost_if_wrong: The boss's LR is validated by measurement before the real run starts; ours is a table lookup that was never tested against an alternative. On 59469903 we shipped 2.86e-05 with zero in-run evidence it was right, and finished 9/12 with a 0.0072 gap to rank 1. On a 0.75h task the boss's plan_budget grants a 3-LR validate sweep (540s cap) that we structurally cannot run.
deltas.recommendation: Port run_lr_search wholesale, or the validate-mode subset of it (BOSS lr_search.py:897-957 plus plan_budget). It is the single largest structural gap in this subsystem and it is the boss's own published, title-retaining code — porting it is not adopting an experiment.

deltas.title: We kept the multi-run LR ladder the boss deleted, and its time gate silently discarded our whole LR search
deltas.what: OURS still runs the ancestral state machine: probe run (checking_mode first_time) -> N confirmation runs at different LRs (second_time) -> a final run at the winner. BOSS deleted it and says so in a comment. Our ladder is gated by a wall-clock estimator that returned n<=0 on a 0.75h task, so mode went straight to finish, no confirmation run ever launched, and the LRRT suggestion + confirmation_candidates + BO were all computed and thrown away.

Every LR mechanism downstream of the range test is dead on any task short enough for the gate to trip — which is every task we drew (0.75h, 0.75h, 1.0h). recon/lrrt_pickers_20260905/FINDINGS.md independently recorded the same failure as "probe preempted by the budget".

deltas.title: The boss's computed LR estimator was deleted; we replaced it with the lookup tables its docstring says it replaces
deltas.what: BOSS derives the starting LR from model physics: eta_target * median weight_rms * sqrt(eff_bs/(eff_bs+gradient_noise_scale)) * sqrt(1e9/params), clamped per task type — computed from the validator's own BaselineStats payload, so it works on an anonymised model with no name. OURS has no such function anywhere; our lr_finder.py is a different file with a different job, and the LR comes from family_lr_table / AR-CSV / hardcoded family profiles. We DO read weight_rms (baseline_stats_reader.py:302) but only feed it to telemetry logging and augmentation detection — never to the LR.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/lr_finder.py:1-235 (no compute_lr_from_stats, no estimate_starting_lr — grep over scripts/ returns zero); LR instead from /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/adaptive_config.py:1576-1615 + 1832-1854; weight_rms read but unused for LR at /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/telemetry.py:92-96
deltas.theirs: BOSS/scripts/lr_finder.py:140 compute_lr_from_stats, :252 estimate_starting_lr, :1-19 docstring ("Replaces the SHA256 hash lookup tables that mapped model names to pre-computed optimal learning rates"); called at BOSS/scripts/instruct_config.py:278-288, always-on gate at BOSS/scripts/text_trainer.py:452
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Our LR depends on whether a prior winner happened to train this family+size; theirs depends on the model's actual weights. On the gemma run the table gave 2.86e-05 while the shared size-bucket table both repos carry says 7.5e-5 for that bucket (instruct_config.py:106 ours, BOSS/scripts/instruct_config.py:39) — a 2.6x disagreement resolved by a 3-sample cell rather than by measurement.
deltas.recommendation: Port compute_lr_from_stats + estimate_starting_lr and make it the Tier-0 estimate that the trial search refines. Demote family_lr_table to a sanity-check log. The wire is already half-built: baseline_stats_reader.get_weight_rms exists and is called.

deltas.title: family_lr_table Tier-1 gate admits LOW-ok where the module's own contract says MED-low
deltas.what: The table's docstring states the admission rule; the caller passes a strictly weaker one. CONFIDENCE_RANK ranks LOW-ok=2 below MED-low=3, so cells with n in {2,3} are admitted that the contract excludes. The boss has no lookup table in this slot at all — its equivalent is a computed estimate that cannot have a confidence tier.

Under the module's own gate this cell is rejected and init_lr falls through to the next tier. A 3-sample cell set the rate for a task we lost by 0.0072 nats. Both directions are live: it is also the only thing that saved us from the 8e-6 generic default, which is 9.4x below the shared bucket table.

Fix the contradiction by deciding the tier chain first: adopt the boss's computed estimate as the fallback (delta 3), THEN raise the gate to MED-low as the docstring requires. Changing the gate alone is a regression.

deltas.title: The shipped LRRT picker was measured as the worst of four and still ships as the default
deltas.what: pick_lr defaults to `slope10` — the LR of steepest smoothed descent, divided by 10. Our own 3-curve GPU comparison measured slope10 at 308.6x from the reference (53.5x after our clamp) and 0/3 above the incumbent, versus lossmin at 4.0x/2.9x and 3/3 above. The default was not changed. The boss runs no range test at all, so it has no picker and no picker bias.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/lr_finder.py:38 `name = picker if picker is not None else os.getenv("LRRT_PICKER", "slope10")`; evidence at /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/recon/lrrt_pickers_20260905/FINDINGS.md
deltas.theirs: ABSENT — BOSS/scripts/lr_finder.py has no sweep and no picker; BOSS/scripts/lr_search.py:170 _warmup_curvature_factor is its only measured LR re-centring, and it is bounded to x0.6-1.6 (lr_search.py:167)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Measured live: loki_59469903.txt 11:24:38 logged slope10=5.214e-07 alongside lossmin=1.707e-04 from the SAME curve — a 327x spread decided by an env-var default we have measured to be the bad end. slope10's answer then hit our own floor and was clamped to 1e-6. Every downstream candidate inherits this.
deltas.recommendation: Note the honest complication FINDINGS.md raises: lossmin brackets better but training too HIGH costs +36% vs +2.7% for too low, so distance alone does not settle direction. Decide it with one clean A/B, not by flipping the default. If delta 1 lands, the picker stops mattering — the trial search measures the LR directly and the range test can be deleted.

deltas.title: Our search can only probe at or below the incumbent; the boss's brackets on both sides by construction
deltas.what: confirmation_candidates emits the (clamped) LRRT suggestion, an optional geometric midpoint, and an upward probe gated on `span_decades < 1.0 AND suggestion < incumbent/2`. Because `explored` includes the incumbent, a suggestion far below it makes the span automatically WIDE and suppresses the very probe meant to fix that case — our own docstring at lines 158-164 admits this. The boss's S1 always probes centre-0.30, centre+0.15 and centre+0.30 decades (and pivots low only if a high LR diverges); validate mode probes centre and BOTH extremes; S3 extends past whichever edge wins.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/lr_search.py:135-141 (the gate), :158-164 (the self-documented suppression), :167-178 (the UNBRACKETED warning)
deltas.theirs: BOSS/scripts/lr_search.py:926 `for off in (0.0, -_S1_HALF_RANGE, _S1_HALF_RANGE)`, :942 `highs = (_S1_HALF_RANGE/2, _S1_HALF_RANGE)`, :980-983 (extend past low OR high edge), :897 _extend_validate_edges
deltas.cost_if_wrong: 4 of 4 invocations in the tournament logged UNBRACKETED with the reason "upward probe suppressed: explored span 1.46d >= 1.0d". FINDINGS.md confirms the structural claim: under slope10 EVERY cell is UNBRACKETED. On any task whose table LR is too LOW, the search cannot discover that a higher rate is better — it can only confirm the incumbent or go lower. Given delta 4 admits 3-sample cells, too-low table LRs are exactly the case we need to recover from.
deltas.recommendation: The gate is unfixable as written because `explored` contains the incumbent — remove the incumbent from the span computation, or (better) drop this arithmetic entirely in favour of the boss's fixed +/-0.30 decade S1, which brackets unconditionally and needs no gate.

deltas.title: The range test re-runs on every trainer retry; the boss caches its search result across attempts
deltas.what: Our LRRT gate is `checking_mode == "first_time"` only — it never checks whether state["lrrt_lr"] is already populated, even though line 886 writes it. Every relaunch of train_instruct.py re-sweeps ~100 steps and reloads the model from disk to discard the sweep's weights. The boss checks a cached best_lr (rescaling it by sqrt(bs_new/bs_old) if the batch changed) and skips the search entirely.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/train_instruct.py:729-731 (gate), :886 `_st["lrrt_lr"] = float(_lrrt_lr)` (written, never read by the gate), :899-916 (the mandatory reload)
deltas.theirs: BOSS/scripts/train_instruct.py:568-578 ("Skip LR search if a previous attempt already found the best LR", with sqrt batch rescale), :651-652 (cache write); same at BOSS/scripts/train_dpo.py:386-387, :482
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Four sweeps in one task: 11:23:43-11:24:38 (55s), 11:25:40-11:26:33 (53s), 14:37:42-14:38:37 (55s), 14:39:39-14:40:31 (52s) = 215s of GPU, plus four from-disk model reloads, on a task with a 45-minute budget — and all four returned the identical number, which was then never used. That is roughly 4-5% of each attempt's wall clock burned on a measurement guaranteed to be discarded.
deltas.recommendation: Cheap, self-contained fix independent of everything else: add `and not get_state().get("lrrt_lr")` to the gate at train_instruct.py:729. Do it whether or not delta 1 lands.

deltas.title: Our sweep discovers the OOM boundary and throws the finding away; the boss carries it into training
deltas.what: When our range test OOMs it halves only its OWN local batch (_attempt_bs), reloads the model, and leaves training_args.per_device_train_batch_size untouched — so the trainer then launches at the batch that was already shown not to fit. The boss's search halves the real training batch via dataloader_factory, all-reduces the minimum across ranks, and explicitly carries the reduced batch into the run.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/train_instruct.py:745-747 (_sweep_bs is derived FROM the training batch), :815-838 (_attempt_bs halving loop — never writes back to training_args)
deltas.theirs: BOSS/scripts/train_instruct.py:591-597 (_halve_batch_dataloader mutates training_args.per_device_train_batch_size), :607 (passed as dataloader_factory), :614-624 (all_reduce MIN across ranks), :625-631 ("Lote reduzido durante busca ... (carries to training)")
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Measured on 59469903: 11:25:41 "[lr-search] sweep OOM'd at batch=4 ... retrying at batch=2", and the trainer nonetheless proceeded and died at 11:25:14 (prior attempt) / repeatedly with "torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 18.49 GiB" at step 4 of 1083. The task then burned a full attempt of the 5-attempt retry budget rediscovering, by crashing, what the sweep had already learned 60 seconds earlier.
deltas.recommendation: Feed the surviving sweep batch back into training_args (and into trainer._train_batch_size) before the finally-block reload. Small, local, and it converts an OOM crash into a batch reduction.

deltas.title: DPO and GRPO have no LR search of any kind on our side
