Our train_dpo.py and train_grpo.py contain no lr_search, no lrrt and no LR refinement at all.

deltas.title: FlashAttention decided by an allow-list of 6 families instead of the boss's deny-list
deltas.what: Boss: disable_flash_attention() is a DENY-list — FA is on unless the model is phi-2, falcon-rw, gptneo, bloom or gptoss. Any architecture outside those six — mixtral, gptneox, opt, starcoder2, falcon (non-rw), and every 2026 arch — gets FlashAttention silently DISABLED where the boss keeps it on.

deltas.title: Vocab-aware batch ceiling has no boss counterpart and fired hardest on our worst task

The boss has no vocab-aware logic anywhere in instruct_config.py — it relies on Liger's fused CE to make the logits tensor not exist. The cap fired AFTER the length-scaling already cut 60 to 25, so the two reductions compound.

Combined with the accum cap above this is the single largest divergence in per-step sample count on the task we lost by 0.0072 nats. The cap's evidence base is Qwen-1.5B OOMs from 2026-05-23/27 — runs made with Liger off. Turn Liger on and the evidence may no longer apply.

deltas.title: DPO max_length and max_prompt_length were deleted from the run command template
deltas.what: Boss's DPO template passes --max_length {max_length} --max_prompt_length {max_prompt_length}, values computed in dpo_config from the dataset's p99 (and chosen-length distribution). Our template has neither flag. get_run_cmd substitutes by per-key string replace, so any max_length adaptive computes for a DPO task is silently dropped — the key has no placeholder to land in. We instead resolve it inside the trainer as min(max_position_embeddings, 4096).

The planner's max_length cannot reach a DPO run at all; the trainer's own min(max_pos, 4096) can be 2-4x the boss's p99 value, and DPO holds chosen+rejected+reference simultaneously. No DPO task was drawn this round, so the cost is entirely future — a boss-round DPO task at 4096 with a reference model is a plausible OOM forfeit.

deltas.title: DPO batch is no longer scaled down when max_length rises
deltas.what: Boss scales the DPO bucket batch by 1024/max_length whenever max_length exceeds 1024, with an explicit note that DPO's chosen+rejected pair makes memory scale fast. We deleted that block and pass the raw bucket batch, while simultaneously raising max_length to min(max_pos, 4096) inside the trainer.

deltas.recommendation: Port the boss's _ref_maxlen scaling verbatim into dpo_config.py, keyed on whatever max_length the DPO path actually ends up using.

deltas.title: max_length policy: our p95 vs the boss's p99 with a 2x-p50 packing floor
deltas.what: Boss: target = max(p99, 2*p50) * 1.1, aligned up to 64, ceiling = model_max_position when it exceeds 2048 (so it can go ABOVE 2048), floor 128. Ours (live): min(4096, max(1024, p95*1.1)), then the validator-halve rule. On the gemma task our own log gives full_seq_p95=2204 and full_seq_p99=2730 — we chose 2424; the boss's formula gives >=3008. Axolotl DROPS over-length rows rather than truncating, so our len-check recorded 746/25977 train rows (2.9%) and 35/1000 dev rows (3.5%) discarded at the cap.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/adaptive_config.py:127-172 and 1910-1918
deltas.theirs: scripts/adaptive_max_length.py:57-86; wired at scripts/instruct_config.py:290-320
deltas.cost_if_wrong: 2.9% of training rows and 3.5% of dev rows thrown away, and the dev rows dropped at a different rate than the train rows — which biases the very gauge checkpoint selection reads. The boss's p99 target would drop under 1%. Answering the brief's question: the boss truncates to a percentile, our LIVE path also truncates to a percentile (a lower one); the competitor's 'take the evaluator's 4096' policy is what our DEAD legacy code does at instruct_config.py:20-38, not what ran.
deltas.recommendation: Port the boss's p99 + 2*p50 target and its 64-alignment. It is a one-line policy change with a measurable effect (row drop rate) that we can verify offline against the same baseline_stats.

deltas.title: Batch-vs-length scaling uses reference 1024 where the boss uses 2048
deltas.what: Both sides shrink batch when max_length exceeds a reference length. Boss: ratio = 2048/max_length, applied only above 2048. Ours: ratio = BUCKET_REFERENCE_LEN(1024)/max_length, applied above 1024. At the measured max_length 2424 ours multiplies the bucket by 0.42 (60→25); the boss's rule at the same length would not fire at all, and at its own ~3008 would multiply by 0.68.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/adaptive_config.py:188 (BUCKET_REFERENCE_LEN = 1024), 1418-1423
deltas.theirs: scripts/instruct_config.py:310-320 (default_max = 2048)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: A systematic ~2x batch reduction relative to the boss on every task whose max_length lands between 1024 and 3000 — which is most of them. The 1024 reference is explicitly labelled an assumption in our own comment, not a measurement.
deltas.recommendation: Measure: the buckets were inherited from the boss lineage, and the boss's own compensation code names 2048 as the length they were fitted at. That is stronger evidence than our stated guess of 1024. Align to 2048 unless a run says otherwise.

deltas.title: Instruct warmup has no total-steps clamp; boss refines it to 3% of planned steps
deltas.what: Boss passes a time-aware ceiling warmup_steps = max(10, min(200, int(hours*60))) and then, inside the trainer, clamps it: warmup = min(warmup_steps, max(10, int(0.03 * total_steps_all_epochs))). Ours passes a fixed 35 (env INSTRUCT_WARMUP_STEPS) plus a sqrt(depth) override, and our train_instruct.py contains ZERO occurrences of the string 'warmup' — the 3% refinement is simply absent. Measured on gemma: we warmed up over 44 steps of 2169 (2.0%); the boss's rule would give min(105, 65) = 65 (3.0%).

deltas.theirs: scripts/instruct_config.py:200-201,208; scripts/train_instruct.py:433-434

Large at the ends of the range: on a short 300-step run our fixed 44 is a 15% warmup where the boss would use 10; on a long 5000-step run the boss warms 150 and we still warm 44. The brief's framing (35 vs a time-aware 200) overstates it — the boss's ceiling almost never binds because the 3% clamp dominates.

deltas.title: min_lr_rate 0.15 for the gemma and phi families vs the boss's flat 0.25

Our per-family floors are exactly the unvalidated adaptive-schedule pattern the validator named as harmful, applied to the task we lost by 0.0072.

deltas.title: family_lr_table admitted at LOW-ok against its own module's stated gate
deltas.what: adaptive_config gates Tier-1 family LR at min_conf="LOW-ok" (n in {2,3}); family_lr_table's own docstring says 'Only apply Tier 1 if confidence >= MED-low'. A 3-sample cell set gemma to 2.86e-05. The boss has no lookup table at all: find_lk_lr is always True (text_trainer.py:454), and instruct always overrides the bucket LR with estimate_starting_lr — a formula (eta_target 0.003 * weight_rms * noise_factor * sqrt(1e9/params)), clamped to [1e-6, 1e-3), computed from the validator's own weight statistics. Notably the boss's instruct path does NOT clamp to the bucket (its DPO path does: min(lr, config["lr"])).
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/adaptive_config.py:1606; /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/family_lr_table.py:34
deltas.theirs: scripts/lr_finder.py:32-64 (_TASK_CONFIG), 140-231 (compute_lr_from_stats); wired at scripts/instruct_config.py:277-287

But the size of the harm is smaller than the '2.6x below the bucket' framing suggests: with a typical weight_rms ~0.02 the boss's own formula gives 0.003*0.02*sqrt(1e9/2.8e9) = ~3.6e-5 before the gradient-noise factor, i.e. the same decade as our 2.86e-5. deltas.title: GRPO beta 0.04 (env-overridable) vs the boss's 0.5
deltas.what: Our live path sets the GRPO KL coefficient to 0.04, citing two winners' training_args.bin extractions from 2026-05-04. The boss sets 0.5 — 12.5x higher. The GRPO score is reward minus 0.5*KL against the base model, so beta is a direct lever on the scored term. Our legacy path additionally has a >=7B floor of 0.10 and a reward_classifier that can overwrite beta entirely.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/adaptive_config.py:2337; /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/grpo_config.py:296,467-470
deltas.theirs: scripts/grpo_config.py:281
deltas.cost_if_wrong: No GRPO task was drawn this round, so zero cost so far. Forward cost is a whole task: 12.5x less KL anchoring means far more drift from the reference, and the drift is subtracted from the score directly. Both values claim empirical grounding; only one of them belongs to the participant who retained the title.
deltas.recommendation: Measure before changing — this is the one delta where a single controlled run settles it, because the metric is computable offline against the frozen base. Until then, treat 0.04 as unvalidated against the boss and consider 0.5 the baseline to beat.

deltas.title: GRPO reward_classifier overrides LR and beta unconditionally because the Tier-1 gate is dead
deltas.what: grpo_config.py:14 sets module-level allow_find_lk_lr = False, so the Tier-1 lookup at line 395 never runs and lookup_hit is permanently False. The Tier-1.5 reward_classifier block is gated on `if not lookup_hit`, so it runs on EVERY GRPO task with reward functions and overwrites both learning_rate and beta from a static 13-function catalog. The boss has no classifier and no such override path.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/grpo_config.py:14, 393-441
deltas.theirs: ABSENT

Note this only affects the legacy path; check whether adaptive's GRPO branch (adaptive_config.py:2400-2415) has the same shape.

deltas.title: Dev split: exact prompt-hash buckets vs the boss's MinHash LSH plus stratification
deltas.what: Boss: stratified_split() near-dedups with MinHash LSH (64 hashes, 16 bands, Jaccard 0.8), makes each duplicate group atomic across the split, then stratifies on a 4x4 grid of length x output-length quantiles, with dev_size = min(1000, max(min(400, n/5), n/33)). Ours: leak_safe_split() buckets rows by a sha1 of the casefolded, punctuation-stripped prompt fields — exact-match only, no similarity — with dev_size = 5% clamped to [64, 1000]. Measured on gemma: our split collapsed 3 buckets out of 26977 (i.e. behaved as a plain random split) while our own dedup crosscheck logged validator near_duplicate_rate = 0.1230.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/data/split_policy.py:88-104 (leak_key), 104+ (leak_safe_split); called at scripts/tokenize_instruct.py:222-235
deltas.theirs: scripts/val_split.py:74-146 (LSH), 163-303 (stratified_split); called at scripts/tokenize_instruct.py:188,212
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Every selection signal we act on reads dev loss — best-checkpoint promotion, early stop, the WSM pool, DPO LR selection. With 12.3% near-duplicates left straddling the split, the dev number is partly measuring memorisation, and cross-miner dev losses are not comparable at all. Our own module docstring states this reasoning and then implements the weaker mechanism.
deltas.recommendation: Port val_split.stratified_split. It is 300 self-contained lines with no new dependency (numpy only), it is the retained champion's version, and its effect is verifiable offline on the archived round-1 datasets before they expire 2026-08-31.

Ours has data/dedup_knn.py doing exact-hash dedup only, with the Jaccard leg measured OFF on the gemma run (jaccard_threshold: None, jaccard_removed: 0, exact_removed: 3 of 26980).

deltas.title: GRPO trains at beta=0.04; the boss trains at beta=0.5, the validator's own KL weight
deltas.what: The scored GRPO metric is weighted reward − 0.5·KL(finetuned‖base) — our own customized_trainer.py:1629 pins BETA_GRPO=0.5 to validator/core/constants.py, and the boss hardcodes the same 0.5 in customized_trainer.py:351 for checkpoint selection. The boss then TRAINS with GRPOConfig beta=0.5, so the training objective is the scoring objective. We train with beta=0.04 (a 12.5x weaker anchor to the reference model) on both paths, then select checkpoints on reward−0.5·KL. That only lets us pick a point on a trajectory chosen by a different objective — the exact argument our own kl_trainer_mixin.py:12-19 makes for instruct KL. Two further mechanisms can move our beta further from 0.5: reward_classifier overwrites it (adaptive_config.py:2408) and a 7B+ floor lifts it only to 0.10 (grpo_config.py:462-470).
deltas.ours: scripts/grpo_config.py:296 ("beta": 0.04); scripts/adaptive_config.py:2337 (ADAPTIVE_BETA_OVERRIDE default 0.04); scripts/train_grpo.py:72 (module constant named BETA_GRPO = 0.04, unused, shadowing the validator's name)
deltas.theirs: scripts/grpo_config.py:281 ("beta": 0.5); scripts/customized_trainer.py:351 (VALIDATOR_BETA_GRPO = 0.5)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: On the boss round's GrpoTask, a policy that drifts 12x further from the reference than the metric permits. The KL term is subtracted at 0.5 weight, so any reward gain bought with drift is eaten before scoring. GRPO is winner-takes-all-ish on rank, and our repo has never scored a GRPO task above rank 1 in any recon'd tournament.
deltas.recommendation: Revert to beta=0.5 as the default in grpo_config.py:296 AND adaptive_config.py:2337, and gate reward_classifier's beta override off entirely (keep its LR suggestion if you want). Rename or delete train_grpo.py:72's BETA_GRPO=0.04 — a dead constant carrying the validator's name with the wrong value is a trap for the next reader.

deltas.title: We force ZeRO-3 + gradient checkpointing on DPO/GRPO where the boss forces neither
deltas.what: The boss's ZeRO-3 DPO buckets all carry "gradient_checkpointing": False, so args.gradient_checkpointing is False, HF's Trainer never re-applies gradient_checkpointing_kwargs inside _inner_training_loop, and the model-level reentrant enable at boss train_dpo.py:227 survives — ZeRO-3 works with reentrant checkpointing. Its GRPO_CONFIG has no "ds" bucket at any size (0_1_b through 40_80_b are all "ddp"; 20B+ uses use_4bit + use_vllm False instead), so boss GRPO never enters ZeRO-3. Our adaptive path (default ADAPTIVE_MODE=1) sets distributed="ds" whenever param>9e9 and gpu_count>1 AND hardcodes gradient_checkpointing="True" for all three task types, which is what makes the use_reentrant flag load-bearing in the first place. Note our LEGACY dpo_config.py:218-219 still honours the boss's gradient_checkpointing=False for ds buckets — only the adaptive path overrides it.
deltas.ours: scripts/adaptive_config.py:2203-2204 (distributed="ds" if param>9e9 and gpu>1; gradient_checkpointing="True"); scripts/train_dpo.py:349-352 and scripts/train_grpo.py:477-480 at HEAD (use_reentrant=bool(zero3)); at 12b16b5 the same lines read {"use_reentrant": False} unconditionally
deltas.theirs: scripts/dpo_config.py:46,54,62,70,78 (gradient_checkpointing False on every ds bucket); scripts/grpo_config.py:13-105 (no bucket sets distributed "ds"); scripts/train_dpo.py:265 and scripts/train_grpo.py:445 ({"use_reentrant": False} unconditional — safe only because the block is unreachable under ds)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: At 12b16b5 — the commit that RAN — a >9B DPO or GRPO task on >1 GPU dies with CheckpointError before step one. No checkpoint is written, the relaunch ladder only pattern-matches OOM, and add_random_noise ships a noised base model: a forfeit, not a bad score. The boss round guarantees a 35-71B task.
deltas.recommendation: Adopt the boss's shape rather than only our flag fix: make adaptive_config.py:2204 emit gradient_checkpointing=False whenever it emits distributed="ds", and stop routing GRPO to "ds" at all until a multi-GPU GRPO run has actually executed. Keep the HEAD use_reentrant fix as belt-and-braces, but do not let it be the only thing standing between us and a forfeit — 4723787 is unpushed and has never been gate-tested.

deltas.title: tokenize_dpo warns about identical chosen/rejected pairs instead of removing them
deltas.what: The boss filters the dataset so no pair where chosen == rejected survives, and logs how many were dropped. We sample the FIRST TEN rows, count identical pairs among them, print "CRITICAL: ... causing random predictions", and then keep every one of them in the training set. An identical pair contributes zero preference signal to the DPO loss and pure noise to the gradient; the validator's DPO eval_loss is measured on real preference pairs.
deltas.ours: scripts/tokenize_dpo.py:122-141 (sample_size = min(10, len(dataset)); prints only, no filter)
deltas.theirs: scripts/tokenize_dpo.py:122-127 (dataset = dataset.filter(lambda ex: ex[chosen_field] != ex[rejected_field]) with a removal count logged)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Every degenerate pair in the DpoTask dataset is trained on. The damage scales with how many the validator's generator emits — unknown, but our own code calls it "CRITICAL" and then does nothing, so we cannot even see the rate in a log because we only look at ten rows.
deltas.recommendation: Port the boss's filter verbatim into tokenize_dpo.py, keep the count in the log, and delete the ten-row sampler. This is a two-line change with no interaction with anything else.

deltas.title: Our KL trainer has no full-fine-tune reference; the boss has one
deltas.what: Both sides take base logits from disable_adapter() under LoRA. The boss ALSO loads a frozen bf16 copy of the original model when the run is full-FT, placed on the training rank's device, and wires it after the LR search to keep it out of OOM-sensitive memory. We have no second source: when the model exposes no disable_adapter we return None and fall back to plain cross-entropy while the task is still scored weighted. So the answer to "does the boss have the fallback-to-CE failure mode ours guards against" is inverted — the boss has no such mode because it has a second reference; our guard exists because we created the hole. Our compensating mechanism, forcing LoRA on every KL task regardless of size, lives only in the adaptive path.
deltas.ours: scripts/kl_trainer_mixin.py:64-67 (returns None with no disable_adapter) and :88-96 (silent plain-CE fallback); scripts/adaptive_config.py:106-108 (_select_lora_config forces LoRA at any size when use_kl)
deltas.theirs: scripts/kl_trainer.py:43-69 (load_base_model) and :117-125 (lazy co-location of the frozen base); scripts/train_instruct.py:840-844 (wired for the not-use_lora case)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Whenever the LoRA forcing does not apply — the legacy-config cascade, or any future path that full-FTs a KL-flagged model — we train plain CE against a KL-weighted score and nothing in the run looks wrong. The boss keeps the exact objective in that case.
deltas.recommendation: Port load_base_model and the not-use_lora branch. It is ~30 lines, it is the boss's own tested code, and it removes the dependency of a scoring-critical objective on one config decision going right.

deltas.title: Our KL objective reaches the trainer only if adaptive_config succeeds; the boss reads the env directly
deltas.what: The boss reads USE_KL / KL_COEF straight from os.environ at the top of the training script, so the KL term is active no matter which config module built the command line. Ours reads train_request["use_kl"], a key set in exactly one place — adaptive_config, at the end of get_adaptive_training_json. text_trainer has an explicit cascade that falls back to legacy instruct_config when adaptive crashes or fails its sanity check; on that path the key is simply absent, _use_kl is False, and both the composite objective and the weighted checkpoint metric silently switch off on a task the validator is scoring with KL.
deltas.ours: scripts/train_instruct.py:560 (_use_kl = bool(train_request.get("use_kl"))); scripts/adaptive_config.py:2794 (the only writer); scripts/text_trainer.py:991-1014 (cascade to legacy that drops it)
deltas.theirs: scripts/train_instruct.py:210-221 (use_kl / kl_coef read from os.environ in the trainer itself)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: A KL-flagged boss-round instruct or chat task that trips the adaptive-safety cascade trains and selects on plain eval_loss while being ranked on eval_loss + kl_coef·KL. The failure is silent — the loss curve is healthy.
deltas.recommendation: Read the environment in train_instruct.py as the source of truth (keep the train_request keys as an audit trail), so the KL decision cannot be lost by a config-path fallback. One-line change, removes a whole failure class.

deltas.title: Our KL term is not divided by gradient-accumulation steps; the boss forces the division path
deltas.what: The boss forces model_accepts_loss_kwargs = False on its KL trainer, with an explicit comment: in transformers>=4.46 training_step SKIPS the loss/grad_accum division when that flag is True, because it assumes the model's loss already divided by the window-global num_items_in_batch. Our mixin delegates CE to super().compute_loss (which, with the flag True, returns the num_items-normalised sum) and then adds kl_coef * kl where kl is a plain per-microbatch MEAN. The two terms are on different scales and no division follows, so over an accumulation window of G microbatches the effective KL coefficient is G times what the task specified. Our adaptive planner emits grad_accum up to 4.
deltas.ours: scripts/kl_trainer_mixin.py:50-56 (__init__ never touches model_accepts_loss_kwargs) and :77,:100 (super() CE + mean KL); scripts/adaptive_config.py:2057-2060 (grad_accum = min(4, max(1, 64 // total_batch)))
deltas.theirs: scripts/kl_trainer.py:94-103 (self.model_accepts_loss_kwargs = False, with the reasoning written out)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: On a KL task with grad_accum=4 we optimise eval_loss + 4·kl_coef·KL instead of eval_loss + kl_coef·KL — over-anchored to the base model, under-fitting the task, on a metric where the coefficient was drawn deliberately. Only correct when grad_accum happens to be 1.
deltas.recommendation: Either set self.model_accepts_loss_kwargs = False in KLWeightedTrainerMixin.__init__ exactly as the boss does, or compute CE manually as the boss does. Do not ship the mixin on a KL task until this is fixed.

deltas.title: Our KL masks after the softmax and needs chunking; the boss masks first and never blows up
deltas.what: The boss selects logits[mask] BEFORE the log_softmax, so the KL math runs on an [N, V] tensor of completion tokens only. We log_softmax the full [batch, seq, vocab] tensor and mask afterwards, which is why kl_objective needed a 187-line module with a chunked walker (KL_CHUNK_ELEMENTS = 2**27) added after a 13 GiB allocation failure on a 135M model. The per-token values are identical either way. We also compute in float32 where the boss stays in the model's native bf16 — that part is a defensible precision choice, but it doubles the memory of a tensor we should not have been materialising at all.
deltas.ours: scripts/kl_objective.py:68-76 (kl_per_token over the full tensor), :79-105 (kl_per_token_chunked, the workaround), :119-124 (mask applied after)
deltas.theirs: scripts/kl_trainer.py:156-168 (mask = labels != -100; sel_ft = logits[mask]; sel_base = base_logits[mask]; softmax on [N, V])
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Memory pressure and a chunking path that only exists to survive our own ordering. On an OOM the caller falls back to an unweighted metric, which our own docstring says silently corrupts checkpoint selection.
deltas.recommendation: Re-order to mask-then-softmax as the boss does, keep the float32 cast on the selected [N, V] tensor, and delete kl_per_token_chunked and its constant. Net simplification and strictly less memory.

deltas.title: Dev absorption never runs on DPO or GRPO — it reads an instruct-only filename
deltas.what: The boss runs its dev pass INSIDE train_dpo.py, at the end of trainer.train(), through run_dev_pass on the DPO trainer (so the loss is the proper chosen/rejected + reference loss). Ours runs in text_trainer AFTER the training subprocess exits and reads a hardcoded path, datasets/dev_tokenized_{task_id}.json. text_trainer's own table says that filename belongs to INSTRUCTTEXTTASK and CHATTASK; DPO writes dpo_dev_{t}.json and GRPO writes grpo_dev_{t}.json. So on DPO and GRPO the open() raises, the except swallows it, and the log prints "[dev-absorb] skipped" — a guaranteed no-op on two of the four boss-round task types.
deltas.ours: scripts/text_trainer.py:1354 (_dev_path = ... f"dev_tokenized_{args.task_id}.json") against scripts/text_trainer.py:170-173 (the per-task filename table); scripts/dev_absorption.py (single instruct-shaped tokenised-rows implementation)
deltas.theirs: scripts/train_dpo.py:545-575 (from dev_pass import run_dev_pass, invoked in-trainer with the DPO batch shape and matched grad-accum)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: The champion publishes devfit,absorb= on every task; our own measurement of the mechanism is −0.0194 on 28c9f3bb and −0.0052 on 3a6658eb, and 21 of 44 adjacent-rank gaps on the recon'd boards are smaller than that. On DPO and GRPO we bank none of it, and the skip is invisible in a log full of other skips.
deltas.recommendation: Either extend absorb_dev_split to take the per-task dev filename from the same table text_trainer.py:170-173 already owns (and handle the DPO/GRPO row shapes), or port the boss's in-trainer run_dev_pass into train_dpo.py. Until then, stop describing dev absorption as a repo-wide mechanism — it is instruct/chat only.

deltas.title: Adaptive warmup is a dead wire on DPO and GRPO — the templates hardcode 35
deltas.what: adaptive_config computes a warmup and puts it in run_config["warmup_steps"], and the substitution loop replaces {key} placeholders in the run_cmd template. instruct_config's template has {warmup_steps}. Ours for DPO and GRPO have the literal 35, so the placeholder does not exist, the substitution finds nothing, and the computed value is silently dropped. The boss has {warmup_steps} in all three templates AND refines it in the training script to 3% of total steps. We deleted that refinement from both train_dpo.py and train_grpo.py.
deltas.ours: scripts/dpo_config.py:163 and scripts/grpo_config.py:218 (--warmup_steps 35 literal); scripts/adaptive_config.py:2206 (the value that never arrives); scripts/instruct_config.py:234 (proof the placeholder form exists in this repo)
deltas.theirs: scripts/dpo_config.py:162 and scripts/grpo_config.py:213 ({warmup_steps}); scripts/dpo_config.py:229-231 and grpo_config.py:259-261 (time-aware value); scripts/train_dpo.py:288-291 (3%-of-total refinement)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Every DPO and GRPO run warms up for exactly 35 steps regardless of budget, dataset size or step count. On a short GRPO run that is a large fraction of training spent below the target LR; on a long DPO run it is negligible. Either way the planner's number is thrown away and the log does not say so.
deltas.recommendation: Restore {warmup_steps} in both templates. This is the same disconnected-wire class as the step-budget and max_length findings; grep the other templates for literals sitting where a placeholder should be before shipping.

deltas.title: GRPO max_prompt_length is pinned at 512 on both our paths; the boss derives it from the data
deltas.what: train_grpo truncates every prompt to train_request.get("max_prompt_length", 512) before training. The boss computes that value from the dataset's own prompt_length_distribution and writes it into train_request, and separately scales the batch down when the resulting sequence exceeds the TRL reference of 1024. We deleted both from grpo_config, and adaptive_config never sets the key at all — so under ADAPTIVE_MODE and under the legacy fallback alike the default 512 is what runs.
deltas.ours: scripts/train_grpo.py:486-491 (get with default 512, then truncate_prompts on train and dev); scripts/grpo_config.py (the boss's max_prompt_length block deleted); scripts/adaptive_config.py (no writer for max_prompt_length — grep returns nothing)
deltas.theirs: scripts/grpo_config.py:293-308 (compute_max_length on prompt_length_distribution, written to train_request) and :344-357 (batch scaled with prompt length)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Any GRPO task whose prompts run past 512 tokens is trained on truncated prompts, so the reward functions score completions to a question the model only half saw. The validator does not truncate. Silent — truncate_prompts logs a duration, not a count.
deltas.recommendation: Set max_prompt_length from the dataset in adaptive_config (or restore the boss's grpo_config block), and at minimum log how many prompts truncate_prompts actually shortened so this is visible next time.

deltas.title: GRPO train/dev split is still shuffle-plus-first-200; the boss stratifies all three task types
deltas.what: We built data/split_policy.leak_safe_split and wired it to instruct (INSTRUCT_SPLIT_POLICY) and to DPO (DPO_SPLIT_POLICY, with a comment explaining why DPO needs it most). GRPO got neither our policy nor the boss's. The boss's val_split.py is explicitly documented as used by tokenize_instruct, tokenize_dpo AND tokenize_grpo, and gives all three MinHash near-dedup, length stratification and a proportional dev size of min(1000, max(min(400, n//5), n//33)) instead of a fixed 200.
deltas.ours: scripts/tokenize_grpo.py:34 (dev_items = data[:dev_size], dev_size default 200) — no policy import, no gate
deltas.theirs: scripts/tokenize_grpo.py:27,43-50 (val_split.stratified_split with proportional dev_size); scripts/val_split.py:1-10 (module docstring naming all three consumers)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: On a large GRPO dataset a 200-row dev set cannot separate candidates that differ in the fourth decimal — which is the margin our checkpoint selection (reward−0.5·KL plateau detection) is reading. On a small one it is a huge holdout. Near-duplicates can straddle the split and inflate the dev signal both ways.
deltas.recommendation: Wire leak_safe_split into tokenize_grpo.py behind a GRPO_SPLIT_POLICY gate, matching what tokenize_dpo.py already does. If that is not affordable, at minimum adopt the boss's proportional dev_size formula — that alone is four lines.

deltas.title: train_dpo shrank 584->451 by dropping the boss's DPO LR search and its DDP safety
deltas.what: The boss runs a full LR search on the DPO path with machinery that only exists because DPO is hard: it disables accelerator.gather_for_metrics during the search (DPOTrainer's get_batch_loss_metrics fires 8+ NCCL all-gathers per training_step, and a rank-local termination condition then deadlocks DDP), all_reduce(MIN)s the batch size after any rank OOM-halves, broadcasts both the chosen LR and the weights from rank 0, caches the result for OOM retries with sqrt batch-scaling, and then does time-aware epoch planning from the measured t_per_step. We deleted all of it and replaced it with a probe_eval_fn that scores LR probes on held-out DPO loss — a good idea, but it is a callback hook for the relaunch-probe mechanism, not an in-run search, and it carries none of the collective-safety reasoning.
deltas.ours: scripts/train_dpo.py:418-427 (the entire replacement: DPO_PROBE_EVAL + probe_eval_fn)
deltas.theirs: scripts/train_dpo.py:371-537 (search, gather_for_metrics disable, batch all_reduce, LR+weight broadcast, state cache, epoch planning)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: On a multi-GPU DPO task we have no in-run LR correction at all — the LR is whatever adaptive_config guessed, and our own gap list already flags DPO LR selection as critical. Worse, the NCCL-collective reasoning the boss wrote down is gone from our tree, so the next person who adds any rank-dependent loop to the DPO path will rediscover the deadlock the expensive way.
deltas.recommendation: Do not port the whole search blind — the validator's report twice named LR machinery as harmful. Do port the DDP-safety comments and the all_reduce(MIN) batch sync into train_dpo.py even if the search stays out, and verify the probe_eval_fn hook is actually reached on a DPO run (checking_mode is set in text_trainer, not in train_dpo).

deltas.title: reward_classifier.py overrides GRPO learning rate and beta from an unvalidated static catalog, on by default
deltas.what: 390 lines, ours only, with no boss counterpart. It fingerprints a task's reward-function mix against a hand-written catalog of 13 functions and returns an LR and a beta, which adaptive_config applies as Tier 1.5. Its own header says it was ported from a friend's R&D and justified by one third-party's bad GRPO result. Default-on (TRAINING_REWARD_CLASSIFIER_ENABLED defaults true). It is the mechanism that can push beta away from 0.5, and it is exactly the shape both validator diff reports condemned: accumulated machinery whose benefit was never measured on our own harness.
deltas.ours: scripts/reward_classifier.py:1-6 (provenance) and :50+ (REWARD_CATALOG); scripts/adaptive_config.py:2400-2410 (applies learning_rate and beta); scripts/grpo_config.py:406-436 (the legacy-path copy)
deltas.theirs: ABSENT — the boss's GRPO LR comes from the size bucket alone (grpo_config.py:13-105) and beta is the constant 0.5
deltas.cost_if_wrong: An unmeasured heuristic silently replaces two of the three hyperparameters that decide a GRPO task, including the one that aligns training with scoring. If it is wrong we cannot tell, because we have no GRPO baseline of our own to compare against.
deltas.recommendation: Flip the default to off (TRAINING_REWARD_CLASSIFIER_ENABLED=0) before the boss round, and at minimum strip its beta authority permanently. Turning it back on requires an A/B on our harness, per the same rule dev_absorption was held to.

deltas.title: No quiet_mode: we publish our strategy to the tournament's public logs
deltas.what: Every boss entrypoint — train_dpo, train_grpo, tokenize_dpo, tokenize_grpo, tokenize_instruct, train_instruct, text_trainer — imports quiet_mode as its very first statement, before any heavy import, which no-ops print() to stdout, forces library log levels to ERROR and disables tqdm, while deliberately preserving stderr so crashes stay diagnosable and OOM detection keeps working. We have no such module and print everything: chosen LR, adaptive plan lines, dedup stats, split stats, len-check warnings, classifier decisions. Our own recon skill mines exactly these logs out of Grafana Loki to learn what competitors ran.
deltas.ours: ABSENT — scripts/train_dpo.py:1-4 opens with the transformers_runtime import, no quiet gate; the same at scripts/train_grpo.py:1-7 and scripts/tokenize_*.py:1
deltas.theirs: scripts/quiet_mode.py:1-31 (the gate and its rationale); imported first in scripts/train_dpo.py:1, train_grpo.py:1, tokenize_dpo.py:1, tokenize_grpo.py:1, tokenize_instruct.py:1
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Every hyperparameter decision we make is readable by any competitor running the same recon we run. That is a standing information leak, not a one-tournament cost.
deltas.recommendation: Port quiet_mode, but verify first that text_trainer's OOM-retry detection reads stderr and not stdout — the boss's comment says it kept stderr alive precisely for that, and ours may pattern-match on stdout. Test that before enabling it in a tournament.

deltas.title: We removed the boss's non-FA packing path, so packing under eager attention cross-contaminates sequences
deltas.what: The boss carries two packing implementations and a packing_mode switch: pack_data_points_FA when flash attention is available, and pack_data_points_naive (per-sequence position_ids reset, standard 1D mask) when it is not. It also packs the dev set ONLY under FA, with the comment that naive packing allows cross-attention between packed sequences and corrupts eval loss. We deleted pack_data_points_naive and the use_fa flag entirely and always call the FA packer. Our adaptive profiles enable packing, and disable_fa can independently be True.
deltas.ours: scripts/monkeypatch.py (pack_data_points_naive deleted; PackedDataset.__init__ has no use_fa); scripts/train_instruct.py:309-323 (unconditional monkey_patch_packing_for_model + FA packer; dev deliberately left unpacked); scripts/adaptive_config.py:540,568,591,607 ("packing": True profiles)
deltas.theirs: scripts/monkeypatch.py:119-160 (pack_data_points_naive) and :252,:283 (use_fa flag and dispatch); scripts/train_instruct.py:304-350 (packing_mode switch, dev packed only under FA)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: On a ChatTask or instruct task where flash attention is unavailable and packing is on, FA-style packing with eager attention lets packed sequences attend across their boundaries. Training silently learns on contaminated context; nothing in the loss curve shows it. This is the one boss-round task type where the delta bites outside DPO/GRPO.
deltas.recommendation: Either restore the naive packer and gate on the attention implementation the run actually got, or make packing conditional on FA being active — do not leave the combination reachable and unguarded.

deltas.title: DPO max_length: ours is model-derived with an OOM rung, the boss's is data-derived with no rung
deltas.what: Genuine two-way split. We compute max_length at runtime from the model config (min(max_position_embeddings, 4096)) to match the validator's DPO evaluator, and we added resolve_dpo_max_length so the OOM ladder's final sequence-length rung actually reaches DPO — previously that rung was inert, the ladder ended at batch=1, and retries re-ran an identical command until they ran out with no checkpoint. The boss instead derives max_length and max_prompt_length from the dataset's own seq_length and chosen_length distributions and scales the batch down when the sequence is long, but has no OOM rung for length.
deltas.ours: scripts/train_dpo.py:117-172 (resolve_dpo_max_length, OOM rung) and :195-210 (AutoConfig-derived cap, max_prompt_length = max_length // 2)
deltas.theirs: scripts/dpo_config.py:199-227 (compute_max_length from seq_length_distribution, prompt length estimated from chosen_length_distribution, batch scaled at max_length > 1024) and :151-170 (--max_length / --max_prompt_length passed on the CLI)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Keeping ours is right for the forfeit case — the OOM rung converts a no-checkpoint retry loop into a shorter run that finishes. But our max_prompt_length = max_length//2 is arbitrary where the boss's is measured, so a prompt-heavy DPO set gets its prompts cut at an unjustified point.
deltas.recommendation: Keep resolve_dpo_max_length. Port only the max_prompt_length derivation from chosen_length_distribution (boss dpo_config.py:207-215) — it is independent of the rest and replaces a guess with a measurement.

deltas.title: DPO lost checkpoint averaging, adaptive eval frequency and NEFTune; only the NEFTune removal is justified
deltas.what: The boss's DPO path registers AdaptiveTrainingCallback (window-3 checkpoint averaging, in-RAM for unsharded models and disk for sharded), sets an adaptive eval/save cadence from hours_to_complete on final runs, and applies always-on NEFTune with a gradient-noise-driven alpha. We carry none of the three on DPO. The NEFTune removal is documented and evidence-backed in our tree (a cited +50% eval_loss regression on task 96421); the other two are simply absent, and we have no DPO-side substitute for either.
deltas.ours: scripts/train_dpo.py:407-411 (callbacks=[eval_save_callback] only — no averaging callback); scripts/dpo_config.py:210-213 (the NEFTune revert with its cited regression); no adaptive eval cadence anywhere on the DPO path
deltas.theirs: scripts/train_dpo.py:30,333-343 (AdaptiveTrainingCallback), :296-305 (adaptive_eval_steps from hours), :316-325 (NEFTune alpha 1, raised to 5 when gradient_noise_scale > 1.0)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Without an adaptive cadence, DPO eval/save frequency is whatever the static config said, so on a long task we sample the loss curve too coarsely to catch the best checkpoint and on a short one we burn budget evaluating. Without averaging we ship a single noisy point. The NEFTune half costs nothing — that deletion is defended.
deltas.recommendation: Port the adaptive eval-frequency block (boss train_dpo.py:296-305) — it is self-contained, cheap and directly improves checkpoint selection. Leave NEFTune out and keep the citation. Hold checkpoint averaging until the ZeRO-3 question above is settled, since the boss's own averaging-mode choice keys off whether the run is sharded.

deltas.title: Core ML pins are byte-identical to the boss — we carry none of the challenger's upgrade
deltas.what: The eight pins the task named plus every other version line match exactly. Boss lines 1-14: accelerate==1.6.0, bitsandbytes==0.45.4, scipy==1.15.2, sentencepiece==0.2.0, einops==0.8.1, wandb==0.19.10, deepspeed==0.15.4, typer==0.9.0, tensorboard==2.19.0, transformers==4.51.3, liger-kernel==0.5.9, peft==0.15.1, datasets==3.5.0, trl==0.18.0. Ours: identical, same order, same lines. Also identical: requirements.txt (docker/typer, both sides, 2 lines) and scripts/ds_config/ (diff -rq returns nothing). The losing challenger went transformers 5.12.1 / trl 1.0.0 / datasets 5.0.1 / liger 0.8.1 / bitsandbytes 0.50.1; we are on none of them. Confirmed against 12b16b5, not just the worktree: `git diff 12b16b5 -- scripts/training_requirements.txt` is empty.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/training_requirements.txt:1-14
deltas.theirs: scripts/training_requirements.txt:1-14 (identical)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Nothing — this is the delta we do NOT have. The report calls the alternative 'Dependency Version Explosion (HIGH CONFIDENCE: harmful)' and prescribes exactly the stack we already run.
deltas.recommendation: Keep. Do not touch these pins for the LFM2 problem either — the boss cannot load lfm2 on 4.51.3 either and it retained the title, so the forfeit on 29fc1a10 was shared, not a deficit. deltas.title: state_manager rewritten from a file to redis, with a PROCESS-LOCAL fallback that silently breaks a cross-process channel
deltas.what: The boss's state_manager is 21 lines: STATE_FILE = "/tmp/trainer_state.json", get_state() reads it, set_state() writes it. Ours is 80 lines of redis client with, on any failure, `_FALLBACK_STATE: dict = {}` — an in-memory dict scoped to ONE interpreter. The channel is genuinely cross-process on both sides: text_trainer.py writes (ours :1118-1124, :1188, :1239, :1258; boss :521) and the train_instruct.py / customized_trainer.py SUBPROCESS reads (ours train_instruct.py:472, customized_trainer.py:254/418/503; boss train_instruct.py:417/568/650, customized_trainer.py:114/179). A file survives process death; a process-local dict does not. If redis is unreachable our writes in the child are invisible to the parent and every reader gets {} — and our own code comments at customized_trainer.py:421 and :505 show we already went around defending against exactly that {}. The boss cannot have this failure mode at all. It did not fire on 20260907 (grep for '[state_manager] redis' in loki_59469903.txt is empty, so redis was up), which is precisely what makes it a latent one.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/state_manager.py:10-19,42-43,62-63
deltas.theirs: scripts/state_manager.py:4-21 (plain JSON file, no redis, no fallback needed)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: A silent state loss between text_trainer and the training subprocess. The state carries run mode and the wall-clock/deadline bookkeeping the checkpoint logic reads; losing it degrades checkpoint and stop decisions with no error, on a task we cannot re-run.
deltas.recommendation: Revert to the boss's file-based state_manager. It is 21 lines, it is strictly more reliable across processes, and it deletes the redis pin, the redis-server apt package, the entrypoint daemon and the 2-second sleep in one move. If per-run telemetry is wanted, keep redis for callbacks/metrics_callback.py and callbacks/experiment_logger.py only — those are genuinely optional — and leave the control channel on the file.

deltas.title: quiet_mode.py: the boss silences its logs; we print our entire strategy into a publicly queryable log
deltas.what: quiet_mode.py (139 lines) is imported as LINE 1 of every boss entrypoint — text_trainer.py:6, train_instruct.py:1, train_dpo.py:1, train_grpo.py:1, tokenize_instruct.py:1, tokenize_dpo.py:1, tokenize_grpo.py:1, add_random_noise.py:1. It no-ops builtins.print to stdout (keeping stderr and tracebacks), forces library log levels to ERROR and sets TQDM_DISABLE / TRANSFORMERS_VERBOSITY / DATASETS_VERBOSITY etc. before the heavy imports. Its docstring states the purpose plainly: verbosity 'would otherwise leak hints in publicly-visible logs'. We have no equivalent — grep for SN56_QUIET, SN56_VERBOSE, builtins.print, TQDM_DISABLE and TRANSFORMERS_VERBOSITY across scripts/ and trainer/ returns zero hits. The consequence is measured, not theoretical: our 20260907 Loki log is 1,252,839 bytes and contains, verbatim and publicly retrievable, '[adaptive] Tier 1 family_lr HIT: lr=2.8600e-05 conf=LOW-ok n=3 task=instruct arch=Gemma2ForCausalLM', '[adaptive] PLAN: lr=2.86e-05 batch=8 epochs=3 max_len=2424 lora=False grad_accum=4', '[lrrt] suggested_lr=5.21e-06, safe_lr=5.21e-07 (idx=34/77) picker=slope10', '[adaptive] EXP-T hours_budget=1.75h step_time_est=8.7s (measured) -> max_steps_budget=666', '[WSM] merge will be gated on held-out loss'. We know this channel is public because we used it ourselves: recon/tourn_e758aac2d861c378_20260824/loki_3a6658eb_full.json is a competitor's build log we pulled the same way.
deltas.ours: ABSENT (no file; nothing imports a log gate — verified across /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts and /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/trainer)

It is cheap, reversible via SN56_VERBOSE=1 for our own smoke runs, and its numba print-impersonation guard (lines 57-69) is a real trap it already solved.

deltas.title: checkpoint_avg_callback.py: the boss averages checkpoints on a FULL fine-tune; we switch ours off run-wide the moment we see one
deltas.what: The boss's 783-line AdaptiveTrainingCallback picks its mode at train_instruct.py:479-483: `_avg_mode = "disk" if (_sharded or 6*_trainable_bytes > 100e9) else "ram"`, with _stream_average_checkpoints (checkpoint_avg_callback.py:411-455) doing an O(1)-RAM per-tensor uniform average of full model.safetensors across checkpoints for the disk case. So full fine-tune is a supported path, not an excluded one. Ours does the opposite: customized_trainer.py:984-1002 detects the absence of adapter_model.safetensors, prints '[WSM] full fine-tune detected ... disabling WSM run-wide (LoRA-only; full FT averaging not implemented)', sets _wsm_enabled = False and deletes the pool. Our 20260907 gemma log prints 'lora=False' — so on task 59469903, the one we lost by 0.0072, our checkpoint averaging was off for the entire run while the boss's would have been in 'ram' mode (2.8e9 params x 2 bytes x 6 = 33.6GB, well under the 100e9 threshold). The boss also carries three sub-mechanisms we lack entirely: overfit detection with rollback + LR cut + escalating NEFTune (checkpoint_avg_callback.py:34-38, _rollback_and_respond at :519+), and memorized-sample masking after rollback (_drop_memorized_samples at :467-513).
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/customized_trainer.py:988-1002 (full-FT gate) and :284-309 (WSM pool, LoRA-only)
deltas.theirs: scripts/checkpoint_avg_callback.py:411-455 (_stream_average_checkpoints) wired at scripts/train_instruct.py:479-495
deltas.cost_if_wrong: On every full-fine-tune instruct task — which is what INSTRUCT_CONFIG selects for the 0-3B buckets, i.e. most of our draws — we ship a single checkpoint where the boss ships an average. Task 59469903's gap to rank 1 was 0.0072; checkpoint averaging routinely moves numbers of that size.
deltas.recommendation: Port _stream_average_checkpoints and the ram/disk mode selector. It is the single highest-value item in this subsystem: it removes an unconditional capability switch-off on the task class we actually get. Do NOT port the rollback / NEFTune-escalation / memorized-masking half in the same change — that is exactly the unvalidated machinery both reports condemn, and it mutates the training trajectory. Averaging is a pure post-hoc read of checkpoints already on disk and is gated by our existing merge_eval_fn (customized_trainer.py:124) so a bad average cannot ship.

deltas.title: KL trainer: the boss forces model_accepts_loss_kwargs=False to keep grad-accum scaling correct; we do not
deltas.what: The boss's KLRegularizedTrainer sets `self.model_accepts_loss_kwargs = False` at kl_trainer.py:103 with 25 lines of comment explaining why: in transformers>=4.46 training_step SKIPS the loss/grad_accum division when that flag is True, relying on the model having divided by the window-global num_items_in_batch; a hand-computed per-micro-batch mean must therefore take the division path or accumulated gradients are ~grad_accum times too large. Our mixin never sets the flag — grep for model_accepts_loss_kwargs across all of scripts/ returns zero hits. Our compute_loss (kl_trainer_mixin.py:76-110) delegates CE to super() (which forwards num_items_in_batch, so the CE half is normalised for the window) and then adds `self.kl_coef * kl` where kl is instruct_kl_tensor's per-micro-batch mean. Summed over N accumulation micro-batches with no division, the KL term arrives at roughly N times its intended weight while CE arrives correctly. Our 20260907 gemma plan line shows grad_accum=4.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/kl_trainer_mixin.py:76-110 (no flag set anywhere in scripts/)
deltas.theirs: scripts/kl_trainer.py:94-103
deltas.cost_if_wrong: On a KL-flagged instruct task with grad_accum>1, the effective kl_coef is inflated by the accumulation factor — we over-penalise drift from the base model and under-fit the CE the score is mostly made of. Scope is bounded: the validator flags roughly 20% of instruct tasks KL, so this did not decide 20260907 unless 59469903 was KL-flagged (recon/tourn_2ba0f79237bffcf7_20260907/task_59469903.json will say). It is a live trap for the boss round, where our memory records both instruct tasks as KL-eligible.
deltas.recommendation: Fix, and mirror the boss's approach rather than inventing one: either set model_accepts_loss_kwargs=False like kl_trainer.py:103, or divide the KL term by the current accumulation steps. Then pin it — tests/test_kl_validator_parity.py already pins the KL formula but cannot see the accumulation scaling, so add a case that accumulates N micro-batches and asserts the summed gradient matches the single-batch equivalent. Confirm first whether 59469903 carried USE_KL, since that decides whether this is a live bug or a boss-round one.

deltas.title: val_split.py: we have leak control and better sizing, but no length/difficulty stratification
deltas.what: Boss val_split.py (303 lines) does three things: MinHash-LSH near-dedup grouping (64 hashes, 16 bands, Jaccard 0.8, _near_dedup_groups at :74-146) so near-duplicate groups stay atomic across the split; 4x4 quantile stratification on length AND difficulty (:210-248) so dev matches the dataset's distribution; and a dev size of min(1000, max(min(400, n//5), n//33)) set at tokenize_instruct.py:207. Ours (data/split_policy.py:110+) does group-atomic assignment by a normalised prompt-side key (casefold, strip punctuation and accents, collapse whitespace, sha1) — O(n) with no pairwise comparison, and it forces oversized buckets to train. Sizing is 5% clamped to [64,1000] and capped at 25% of data. On the gemma task (n=26980) the two land close: boss 817 dev rows, ours 1000. What we lack is stratification — our dev set is a random draw over buckets, so its length and difficulty distribution can drift from the training set's.

Every selection we make reads dev loss — checkpoint choice, the WSM merge gate, the LR probe scoring at train_instruct.py:653 — so the noise floor of that signal sets the resolution of all of them. Our own calibrated dev-loss noise floor is 0.009, and 59469903's gap to rank 1 was 0.0072, i.e. inside it.
deltas.recommendation: Port the stratification half only — _quantile_bins plus the composite 4x4 stratum sampling (val_split.py:151-160, 198-258) — layered on top of our existing buckets, which already give the group atomicity MinHash is there to provide. Skip _near_dedup_groups: it is O(n * bands) with a pairwise verification step and duplicates what leak_safe_split plus dedup_knn already do. This is a cheap variance reduction on a signal we know is our binding constraint.

deltas.title: data_filter.py: our dedup is better placed, but we have no loss-based outlier filter
deltas.what: The boss's data_filter.py has two halves. deduplicate_samples (:21-55) hashes (input_ids, labels) on the TOKENIZED dataset and is called conditionally at train_instruct.py:262 only when baseline_stats reports near_duplicate_rate > 0.2. filter_outliers (:134-226) computes per-sample loss with a no-grad forward (compute_sample_losses at :58-131) and keeps samples within median +/- 3*MAD, dropping zero-loss rows — used by the rollback path at checkpoint_avg_callback.py:481. Ours is unconditional and earlier in the pipeline, which is the better placement — deduping before the split is what stops duplicates straddling it. We have no MAD outlier filter and no per-sample loss pass at all.

deltas.title: adaptive_max_length.py: we have an equivalent, sized from p95 rather than p99 and not packing-aware
deltas.what: Boss adaptive_max_length.compute_max_length (:27-109) takes seq_length_distribution, uses max(p99, 2*p50) when packing and p99 when not, adds a 10% buffer, aligns to 64, and allows going ABOVE the 2048 default up to the model's max_position_embeddings. Its caller (instruct_config.py:306-320) then compensates batch_size proportionally when max_length rises. Ours is split across two files and both fire: instruct_config.py:20-38 mirrors the validator's auto-halve (4096, or ceil(max_pos/2) when max_pos < 8192) and adaptive_config.py:1268-1290 sizes from full_seq_p95 and applies a p99-based halving rule. It works — our 20260907 log prints '[adaptive] max_length sized from full_seq_p95=2204', '[adaptive] EXP-K2 max_length halving applied: instruct_hp=3072 -> 2424', and '[adaptive] batch bucket scaled for length: 60 -> 25 (max_length=2424 vs reference 1024)', so the data-driven sizing AND the batch compensation both happen. Three real differences: we key on p95 where the boss keys on p99; we are not packing-aware (no max(p99, 2*p50) branch); and we compute this in two places (instruct_config sets train_request['max_length'] at :443, adaptive_config computes its own) where the boss computes it once.

Do resolve the two-site computation — establish which of instruct_config.py:443 and adaptive_config.py's _select_max_length actually wins on the instruct path, because two independent sizings of the same quantity is the shape of the bug class our own memory names ('correct code nothing calls on one path'). deltas.title: Our extra top-level directories cannot reach a tournament run — but recon/ is published if we ever place
deltas.what: The Dockerfile has exactly one COPY: `COPY scripts /workspace/scripts` (ours :50, boss :23). Nothing else enters the image. ops/, tests/, trainer/, mcp_server/, recon/, extract_training_log.sh and pre-submit-smoke-test.sh are therefore invisible to a training run — confirmed twice over: the 20260907 build log shows Step 8/14 as that single COPY, and grep for cross-imports from scripts/ into those trees returns only download_model_only.py:2 importing trainer_downloader, which resolves to scripts/trainer_downloader.py (byte-identical to the boss's) and not to trainer/utils/. There is no .dockerignore on either side, so the full 4.4M recon/ tree is sent to the docker daemon as build context, but 4.4M is negligible build time. The real exposure is different: winner repos are published to gradients-opensource — that is how we are reading this boss's code — and recon/ is 74 tracked files at 12b16b5 containing our competitor analysis, our measured findings (recon/lrrt_pickers_20260905/FINDINGS.md, recon/ab_step_budget_20260904/), harvested competitor Loki logs and the archived diff reports. A tracked-file secret scan over 12b16b5 (hf_/sk- tokens, HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=, WANDB_API_KEY=, PEM headers) returns clean. Two smaller notes: our dockerfile is duplicated at ops/docker/ and dockerfiles/ and cmp confirms the two are byte-identical (tests/test_dockerfile_paths.py guards the drift), and we retain hf-uploader.dockerfile and trainer-downloader.dockerfile which the boss deleted — the latter installs an UNPINNED transformers at :5, but neither is built on the text-tournament path.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/dockerfiles/standalone-text-trainer.dockerfile:50 (the only COPY); /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/recon/ (74 files tracked at 12b16b5)
deltas.theirs: dockerfiles/standalone-text-trainer.dockerfile:23 (the only COPY); boss repo has scripts/ + dockerfiles/ + requirements.txt + utility_models.py and nothing else
deltas.cost_if_wrong: Zero for a run — these directories are provably unreachable from the container. Non-zero for intelligence: if we ever place, recon/ ships to a public GitHub org along with everything we have learned about how the field is scored and what our rivals ran.
deltas.recommendation: Leave them for now — deleting them buys no ranks and costs us our own tooling. Before the submission that could actually win, move recon/ (and its FINDINGS.md files) out of the tracked tree or into a separate private repo. Note the boss did exactly this pruning: its own .gitignore carries a 'Local-only experiment/seeding/trainer helpers (never commit — contain IPs, repo URLs, commit hashes, task IDs)' block, so the champion treats its own recon as something not to publish.

deltas.title: PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True exported in our entrypoint, absent from the boss's
deltas.what: Our entrypoint.sh:9 exports PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True with the comment 'Reduce VRAM fragmentation on multi-GPU + gradient_checkpointing'. The boss's entrypoint (4 lines total) sets no environment at all, and grep across its scripts/ finds no PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF anywhere. It did take effect in the 20260907 run (the string appears once in the Loki log). This is a real allocator behaviour change applied to every task of every type, adopted without a measurement on either side.
deltas.ours: /Users/m1/Documents/lostinjamal/scripts/entrypoint.sh:9
deltas.theirs: ABSENT (scripts/entrypoint.sh:1-4 sets no env; no PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF anywhere in boss scripts/)
deltas.cost_if_wrong: expandable_segments is a well-understood PyTorch allocator mode and is very unlikely to be harmful; it plausibly helps the OOM ladder our memory records us fighting (the max_length fix pushing KL LRRT into OOM). But it is unvalidated machinery applied globally, which is precisely the pattern both reports name, and if it interacts badly with a specific model it will look like an unexplained OOM.
deltas.recommendation: Keep, but stop treating it as free. Put it behind an env with the current value as the default so a suspected allocator interaction can be bisected in one run without rebuilding the image, and record it on the list of unvalidated global settings so it is a candidate the next time an OOM has no other explanation.

verdicts.title: [3] Our KL checkpoint metric costs two extra dev passes per eval; the boss's costs zero
verdicts.why: Placement claim confirmed: ours customized_trainer.py:311-363 called first at :691, kl_metric_fn at train_instruct.py:691-714 loops the eval loader with two forwards/batch, wired :716-717; boss callback compute_loss is metrics.get('eval_loss') at 98-103 with the KL inside KLRegularizedTrainer.compute_loss (kl_trainer.py:127-183, returns (loss, outputs) at :183), wired train_instruct.py:501,534-537. verdicts.title: [4] dev_absorption leaves a stale model.safetensors.index.json in the staged submission
verdicts.why: Three independent reasons this is not a defect. (1) The mechanism description is wrong for the boss. dev_pass.py:178 makes an EMPTY staging dir, :180 save_pretrained writes fresh weights into it, :183-186 copies only NOT-_is_weight_file files back from the old submission — so _is_weight_file (:154-157) is an EXCLUSION filter protecting the freshly written index, not a deletion filter. The analyst's 'both sides stage, delete the old weight files, save fresh weights, then swap' is only true of ours (dev_absorption.py:262-268). (2) The claimed harm cannot occur. In transformers modeling_utils.py the from_pretrained resolution chain checks SAFE_WEIGHTS_NAME (model.safetensors) FIRST and only falls through to SAFE_WEIGHTS_INDEX_NAME (~:935-948), so a leftover index sitting beside fresh single-file weights is never read; and when the new save IS sharded, :4183-4188 rewrites the index. The only surviving case is sharded-original -> unsharded-new, which the loader ignores. (3) The boss's predicate is not the complete one the finding implies — `pytorch_model.bin.index.json` matches neither the literal nor the `.bin` suffix at dev_pass.py:154-157, so the boss carries the identical gap for the torch-format index. verdicts.title: [1] GRPO trains at beta=0.04; boss trains at beta=0.5

verdicts.title: [2] We force ZeRO-3 + gradient checkpointing on DPO/GRPO where the boss forces neither

verdicts.title: [3] tokenize_dpo warns about identical chosen/rejected pairs instead of removing them
verdicts.why: Exact on both sides. Boss tokenize_dpo.py:122-127 is dataset.filter(lambda ex: ex[chosen] != ex[rejected]) with a removal count logged; ours tokenize_dpo.py:122-141 samples min(10, len(dataset)) rows, prints "CRITICAL: ... causing random predictions" and keeps every row. I searched for the behaviour rather than the identifier - recursive grep over scripts/ for any chosen!=rejected comparison, filter or dedup returns nothing outside that print, and tokenize_dpo's only other data operation is leak_safe_split at :91-92, which splits but does not drop. One mechanism correction: for a byte-identical pair all four DPO log-prob terms cancel, so the loss is a constant log 2 and the gradient is exactly zero (nonzero only if dropout is active) - the harm is dilution of the batch and an inflated loss floor, not "pure noise to the gradient". The fix and its size are as described.

verdicts.title: [4] Our KL trainer has no full-fine-tune reference; the boss has one
verdicts.why: The gap is real: boss kl_trainer.py:43-69 load_base_model, lazy co-location at :117-125, wired at train_instruct.py:836-844 (not 840-844) for the not-use_lora case; ours kl_trainer_mixin.py:64-67 returns None with no disable_adapter. The scored metric is still weighted." once, loudly, by design (comment at :102-104). (b) "the boss has no such mode" is wrong: boss kl_trainer.py:78-79 states it falls back to plain CE when neither base source is configured; it just always configures one. A hole the analyst missed strengthens the finding - adaptive_config.py:103-104 returns {"use_lora": False} when param_count is None regardless of use_kl, so an unreadable param count on a KL task gives full-FT, no adapter, and CE-only training. The rec stands.

verdicts.title: [5] Our KL objective reaches the trainer only if adaptive_config succeeds
verdicts.why: Traced completely. train_instruct.py:560 _use_kl = bool(train_request.get("use_kl")); a tree-wide grep shows adaptive_config.py:2794 is the only writer of that key, at the very end of get_adaptive_training_json (:2789-2796). text_trainer's cascade restores the pre-adaptive snapshot on both failure routes - the sanity-check branch (~:989) and the crash handler (:1014), both `train_info = _train_info_snapshot` - so on the legacy path the key never exists, _use_kl is False, and both the composite objective (:562-576) and the weighted checkpoint metric (:688-718) switch off. Boss train_instruct.py:210-221 reads USE_KL/KL_COEF from os.environ in the trainer itself. Two additions: our env reader already exists (kl_objective.py:142 read_kl_config) and is called only from adaptive_config, so the fix is a re-route not new code; and adaptive_config.py:2786-2788 already concedes "the env vars are readable there too".

verdicts.title: [6] Our KL term is not divided by gradient-accumulation steps
verdicts.why: I did not take this from the boss's comment - I verified the mechanism in transformers source (4.57.6 installed; our pin is 4.51.3, both >= 4.46). Trainer.__init__ trainer.py:633-641 sets model_accepts_loss_kwargs from the PEFT-UNWRAPPED forward signature (any VAR_KEYWORD), so a LoRA-wrapped Llama/Gemma/Qwen yields True; compute_loss trainer.py:4105-4109 then injects num_items_in_batch; training_step trainer.py:4060-4064 skips `loss = loss / self.current_gradient_accumulation_steps` precisely when that flag is True. Our mixin's signature kl_trainer_mixin.py:76 takes **kwargs and forwards them to super at :77, so CE comes back num_items-normalised, while :98-100 adds kl_coef * a per-microbatch mean with no compensating division - relative KL weight inflated by G. Boss kl_trainer.py:94-103 sets the flag False with that reasoning written out. adaptive_config.py:2057-2060 grad_accum = min(4, max(1, 64 // total_batch)) confirmed. Caveat worth stating: inert when grad_accum == 1, which is the case whenever batch*gpu_count >= 64.

verdicts.title: [7] Our KL masks after the softmax and needs chunking; the boss masks first
verdicts.why: All lines exact. Ours kl_objective.py:68-77 kl_per_token over the full [batch, seq, vocab] tensor, :79-105 kl_per_token_chunked with KL_CHUNK_ELEMENTS = 2**27 at :65, mask applied at :119-124; the file is 187 lines. Boss kl_trainer.py:156-168 does mask = labels != -100 then logits[mask] before log_softmax, so the softmax runs on [N, V]. Per-token values are identical (log_softmax reduces over vocab, positions independent) and the gradient is equivalent (masked positions multiply to zero in ours, are not selected in the boss's). The 13 GiB OOM justifying the chunker is our own recorded measurement (kl_objective.py:90-92), and it justifies the chunker rather than the ordering - which is exactly the analyst's point. The float32 choice is documented and defended at kl_objective.py:38-41 and correctly called defensible. RISK is the right label; no correctness defect exists here.

verdicts.title: [8] Dev absorption never runs on DPO or GRPO - it reads an instruct-only filename
verdicts.why: Confirmed with one scope correction and one bonus defect. Ours: text_trainer.py:1354 _dev_path = os.path.join("datasets", f"dev_tokenized_{args.task_id}.json") against the TOKENISED_OUTPUTS table at :169-174, which assigns dpo_dev_{t}.json to DPOTASK and grpo_dev_{t}.json to GRPOTASK; dev_absorption.py:147 opens that path and the except at text_trainer.py:1382-1385 swallows the FileNotFoundError as "[dev-absorb] skipped". Boss train_dpo.py:551,565 imports and calls run_dev_pass in-trainer. SCOPE CORRECTION: the boss has no dev pass on GRPO either - grep for run_dev_pass across boss scripts hits train_instruct.py and train_dpo.py only - so versus the boss the true gap is DPO, and GRPO is a gap versus nobody. BONUS DEFECT in the same block: the comment at text_trainer.py:1346 says "Default OFF ... It stays gated until an A/B on our own harness produces ours", while :1351 reads os.getenv("DEV_ABSORPTION", "1") == "1" - default ON. verdicts.title: [9] Adaptive warmup is a dead wire on DPO and GRPO - the templates hardcode 35

Ours dpo_config.py:163 and grpo_config.py:218 both read `--warmup_steps 35`; boss dpo_config.py:162 and grpo_config.py:213 read {warmup_steps}; our instruct_config.py:234 proves the placeholder form exists here. MATERIALITY CAVEAT the analyst did not state: the value that fails to arrive is itself 35 in nearly every profile (adaptive_config.py:520-677), so the live cost is confined to the depth-warmup override (:265-273, e.g. 35 -> 46) and the small-data 15 at :519 - a real dead wire with a small blast radius.

verdicts.title: [12] train_dpo shrank 584->451 by dropping the boss's DPO LR search and its DDP safety
verdicts.why: Facts hold: boss train_dpo.py:371-537 is the whole search (gather_for_metrics disable at :424-425, _halve_batch_dataloader at :409-417, all_reduce(MIN) at :446-462, LR+weight broadcast at :465-476, state cache at :480-485, epoch planning at :487-537); ours train_dpo.py:419-427 is the DPO_PROBE_EVAL replacement; wc confirms 584 vs 451. Both stated reasons are wrong. (a) The collective-safety machinery is a fix for a hazard the boss manufactures - a rank-local search that can run different trial counts and halve batches per rank. Our train_dpo contains zero occurrences of lr_search, all_reduce, gather_for_metrics or broadcast, and never mutates per_device_train_batch_size after args parsing (only reads it at :225,:243,:370), so porting all_reduce(MIN) would import a fix for a problem we deleted. (b) "verify the probe_eval_fn hook is actually reached (checking_mode is set in text_trainer, not in train_dpo)" is refuted: train_dpo.py:399 passes checking_mode=train_request.get("checking_mode", "none") into CustomEvalSaveCallback, which consumes probe_eval_fn at customized_trainer.py:389-393; text_trainer.py:1137-1151 sets the value. The real residue is that the boss's time-aware epoch/warmup/eval re-planning from measured t_per_step sits INSIDE the same else-branch (:487-537), so deleting the search deleted that too.

verdicts.title: [13] reward_classifier.py overrides GRPO learning rate and beta from an unvalidated static catalog, on by default
verdicts.why: 390 lines confirmed; provenance header at :1-6 ("Ported 2026-05-15 from hyper-text ... (friend's R&D)"); REWARD_CATALOG at :49; default-on gate at adaptive_config.py:2356-2357 (TRAINING_REWARD_CLASSIFIER_ENABLED default "true"); it writes learning_rate at :2405 and beta at :2409; the legacy copy is grpo_config.py:411-441 and writes both unconditionally at :434-435. And the ABSENT needs narrowing: the boss is not reward-blind - grpo_config.py:111-113 if_contain_slow_reward_function drives batch size and save_before_remaining_time at :310-337, and we carry the same thing (adaptive_config.py:2319-2327). verdicts.title: [14] No quiet_mode: we publish our strategy to the tournament's public logs
verdicts.why: The absence is real and survives a behaviour search: recursive grep over our scripts/ for builtins.print, TQDM_DISABLE, TRANSFORMERS_VERBOSITY, SN56_QUIET, logging.disable returns nothing. Boss quiet_mode.py is 139 lines (the cited ":1-31" is only its docstring; the print shim is :49-54, the env/log silencing :83-119, the never-raise entry :126-139) and is imported first in EIGHT entrypoints, not seven - the analyst missed add_random_noise.py:1; text_trainer.py:6 is the first import but follows a shebang and docstring, so "very first statement" is imprecise. BONUS, which answers the rec's open question: adopting quiet_mode would NOT break our OOM detection - text_trainer.py:57-64 launches children with stderr=subprocess.STDOUT and matches OOM_ERROR (text_trainer.py:305) = "torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory", a traceback string quiet_mode deliberately preserves on stderr. The real cost is to us: the parent's own echo at text_trainer.py:69 is a print(), so importing quiet_mode in text_trainer blanks the console/Loki stream our forensics depend on while keeping the on-disk log.

verdicts.title: [15] We removed the boss's non-FA packing path, so packing under eager attention cross-contaminates sequences
verdicts.why: The combination is NOT reachable and unguarded - we guard it on BOTH config paths, and the analyst missed both guards. instruct_config.py:347-350: if disable_fa == "True" or architecture is optforcausallm then run_config["packing"] = "False". adaptive_config.py:2680-2686: if disable_fa is true and packing == "True" then packing = "False", with a comment that names this exact bug ("packing without flash-attn lets rows attend across block boundaries") and records that the adaptive path previously lacked it. Both are present at 12b16b5, the commit that ran. So where the boss switches to naive packing we simply stop packing - a throughput trade, not contamination. The mechanism claim is otherwise sound (pack_data_points_FA at monkeypatch.py:134 writes segment ids 1,2,3... as the attention_mask, isolated only by the _get_unpad_data patch at :112, which is a flash-attn path), which is precisely why both configs refuse the combination. The boss citations are also wrong: use_fa is at boss monkeypatch.py:297,302,329, not :252,:283. Residue worth a separate, smaller ticket: on a disable_fa model we lose the boss's ~2-3x naive-packing throughput (boss instruct_config.py:227-233).

verdicts.title: [17] DPO lost checkpoint averaging, adaptive eval frequency and NEFTune
verdicts.why: The headline "we carry none of the three on DPO" is false on two of three. CHECKPOINT AVERAGING is present under another name: WSM top-K averaging lives inside CustomEvalSaveCallback - customized_trainer.py:284-309 (TRAINING_WSM_ENABLED default "1", TRAINING_WSM_TOP_K default 3, the same window of 3 as the boss's), tracked at :954-963, merged at :1044 via :1239, and :223 states it is "Active for Instruct/DPO" and disabled only in the GRPO subclass. train_dpo.py:390-400 builds that callback and passes it at :410, and it drives its own evals through control.should_evaluate (customized_trainer.py:566,680) regardless of the template's --eval_strategy no, so the pool does fill on DPO. ADAPTIVE EVAL FREQUENCY is not absent, it is fixed rather than hours-derived: WhenToEvalHandler (customized_trainer.py:1681-1700) fires at every epoch boundary, every periodic_save_steps=500 (dpo_config.py:252) and at the deadline. The boss's formula (train_dpo.py:297-305, max_evals = max(3, hours*4), eval_steps = max(30, total // min(10, max_evals))) yields a comparable eval count for a 2h run, so "cheap and directly improves checkpoint selection" is unsupported by anything I can read. NEFTune is the one correct sub-claim: absent by documented choice, dpo_config.py:211-214, citing the task 96421 +50% eval_loss regression; boss applies it at :316-325.

verdicts.title: [10] KL trainer: boss forces model_accepts_loss_kwargs=False, we do not
verdicts.why: Reproduced end to end. Boss kl_trainer.py:94-102 is the 9-line comment explaining that transformers>=4.46 training_step skips the /grad_accum division when the flag is True, and :103 is `self.model_accepts_loss_kwargs = False`. LIVENESS genuinely unknown, and the analyst flagged it correctly: no 'kl' string appears in loki_59469903.txt, and recon/.../task_59469903.json carries its own kl_note saying use_kl and kl_coef are never persisted — so whether this was live on 59469903 or is a boss-round bug cannot be settled from what we hold.

verdicts.title: [16] PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True exported in our entrypoint
verdicts.why: Code claims CONFIRMED: our entrypoint.sh:9 exports it with that comment, the boss entrypoint is 4 lines and sets no environment, and PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF appears nowhere in the boss's scripts/. Propagation is real — text_trainer.py:52 does os.environ.copy() before Popen, so the child inherits it. But the EVIDENCE that it took effect is REFUTED. The single occurrence of 'expandable_segments' in loki_59469903.txt is inside PyTorch's own CUDA-OOM boilerplate: '...If reserved but unallocated memory is large try setting PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True to avoid fragmentation. See documentation for Memory Management...'. That is PyTorch suggesting the setting, printed as part of an OutOfMemoryError (the log has 5 OOM hits), not an echo of our export. Nothing in the log confirms the variable was active. The RISK label and the rec (put it behind an env, add it to the unvalidated-globals list) stand — arguably more strongly, since the one place it shows up is an OOM message.
